# affectUI

> Agent-ready React UI for AI products and SaaS: 109 components, screens, blocks, illustrations and motion effects. Every item is one .tsx file with its styles inside – no Tailwind, no animation library, no other dependencies. React 19, dark mode and reduced motion built in.

40 items are free and open source (MIT). The other 69 are part of affectUI Pro, a one-time purchase (https://www.affectui.com/pricing).

## How to add an item

- Free items: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/<slug>.json` – the file lands in components/ui.
- Short names: register `"@affectui": "https://www.affectui.com/r/{name}.json"` under "registries" in components.json, then `npx shadcn@latest add @affectui/<slug>`.
- Pro items: the same commands, with the buyer's access key (AFFECTUI_TOKEN, created under https://www.affectui.com/account/downloads) sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` – set it as a header on the @affectui registry in components.json. Without a key the registry answers 401.
- Import from `@/components/ui/<slug>` and keep the component's own styles and motion; adapt only content and props.
- MCP server: https://www.affectui.com/api/mcp (Streamable HTTP) – search items, read docs and fetch source from Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Codex.


---

## Agent Inbox (Pro)

All your background agent tasks in one calm list – live clocks and status tags, filter tabs with rolling counts, rows that unfold to the last steps with Approve, Reject, Retry or Open, and glide to their new place

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-inbox
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-inbox.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-inbox`

### When to use

- Agent products where several tasks run in the background and people come back to see what finished, what failed and what waits for them
- A sidebar or home screen that collects approvals from many runs in one place, instead of one modal per agent
- Job queues in general – imports, syncs, evaluations – where each job has a short history and one next step

### When not to use

- One single approval in the flow of a chat – use Approval Card
- The plan of one run, step by step – use Agent Plan; for a single tool call use Tool Call Card
- Hundreds of jobs – the list is for a few dozen at most; page or search a bigger queue in a table

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentInbox } from "@/components/ui/agent-inbox";

export function Tasks() {
  return (
    <AgentInbox
      tasks={[
        {
          id: "migrate",
          title: "Migrate users table to Postgres 17",
          agent: "Opus 5.5",
          status: "waiting",
          startedAt: Date.now() - 6 * 60_000,
          steps: [
            { label: "Dry run on staging – no errors", time: "2m ago" },
            { label: "Wants to run it on production", time: "1m ago" },
          ],
        },
        { id: "notes", title: "Write release notes for v2.4", agent: "Sonnet 5.5", status: "running", startedAt: Date.now() - 80_000 },
        { id: "digest", title: "Weekly metrics digest", agent: "Haiku 5.5", status: "done", elapsed: 252_000 },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `AgentTask[]` |  | { id, title, agent, status, startedAt?, elapsed?, steps? } – status is "running", "waiting", "done" or "failed"; steps are { label, time? }, oldest first |
| onApprove | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Approve on a waiting task. Without it the task turns running inside the inbox |
| onReject | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Reject on a waiting task. Without it the task turns failed with the step "Rejected by you" |
| onRetry | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Retry on a failed task. Without it the task runs again and its clock starts over |
| onOpen | `(task: AgentTask) => void` |  | Shows an Open button on running and done tasks |
| filter | `"all" \| "needs-you" \| "running" \| "done"` |  | Controlled filter. Needs you holds waiting and failed tasks |
| defaultFilter | `AgentInboxFilter` | `"all"` | Starting filter when uncontrolled |
| onFilterChange | `(filter: AgentInboxFilter) => void` |  | Called when a tab is picked |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | A button on the tray with a plus, e.g. New task |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: On the tabs: moves to and picks the previous or next filter; Home and End jump to the first and last
- Tab: From the tabs through the rows, then the buttons inside an open row and the tray action
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes a row, presses Approve, Reject, Retry or Open
- Esc: Closes the open row and puts focus back on it

### Accessibility

- The filter is a radio group with one tab stop; each tab's count is part of its name
- Each row is a button with aria-expanded that reads title, agent, time and status; a closed row's details are inert
- Rows hidden by the filter are inert and hidden from screen readers while they fold away
- Status changes are announced politely once ("Write release notes for v2.4: done"); the hover line on the tray stays quiet

### Motion

- Running tasks spin a small blue ring and their clock ticks every second; a waiting task's amber dot breathes slowly
- When a status changes, the glyph pops into its new shape and the tag crossfades in place; after a moment the row glides to its new group (FLIP) or folds away if the filter no longer holds it
- The tab thumb slides to the picked filter; counts roll up or down when tasks change
- Rows open in place to the last steps as a tiny timeline; new steps rise in, new tasks unfold at their spot
- Hovering a tab or a part of the tray line fades the rows it doesn't include; hovering a row tells on the tray what it is doing right now
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 400px. Below 380px the tabs tighten, below 330px the count of All gives way and rows lose a little padding – it works down to 300px
- Touch screens: taller tabs, rows and buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass startedAt for running and waiting tasks so the clock ticks; pass elapsed for finished ones – without it the clock stops where it was when the status changed
- Rows are sorted into groups: waiting, failed, running, done; inside a group they keep your order, so put new tasks first
- With a handler the inbox never changes a status by itself – update the task in your state (e.g. waiting → running → done) and it follows
- Show the last step as what the agent is doing or asking – it is what the tray says when the row is hovered

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: approval-card, agent-plan, tool-call-card, decision-inbox

---

## Agent Lanes (Pro)

Where every agent is right now – a live timeline with a lane per agent, tasks growing into “now”, hand-offs drawn between agents and approvals right on the block

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-lanes
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-lanes.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-lanes`

### When to use

- A team of agents works in parallel and people want to see at a glance who is doing what, and since when
- Multi-agent pipelines where work moves from one agent to the next (research → writing → review)
- A control room for agents: spot the one that waits for a decision, or failed, without opening each run

### When not to use

- A list of background tasks grouped by state – use Agent Inbox
- The steps of one single run – use Agent Plan or Agent Steering
- Scheduling future work on a calendar – the lanes show the last half hour, not the week ahead

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentLanes, type LaneAgent, type LaneTask } from "@/components/ui/agent-lanes";

const agents: LaneAgent[] = [
  { id: "research", name: "Researcher", model: "Opus 5.5" },
  { id: "writer", name: "Writer", model: "Sonnet 5.5" },
];

export function AgentRoom({ tasks }: { tasks: LaneTask[] }) {
  return (
    <AgentLanes
      agents={agents}
      tasks={tasks} // { id, agentId, title, status, start, end?, handoffTo?, ask? }
      onApprove={(task) => api.approve(task.id)}
      onReject={(task) => api.reject(task.id)}
      onOpen={(task) => router.push(`/runs/${task.id}`)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agents | `LaneAgent[]` |  | One lane each: { id, name, model?, avatar? }. A logo as avatar sits on a white tile; without one the initials show. Free agents get an Idle tag, waiting ones Needs you |
| tasks | `LaneTask[]` |  | { id, agentId, title, status: "done" | "running" | "waiting" | "failed", start, end?, handoffTo?, ask?, summary?, tools? }. No end: the block reaches "now" |
| span | `number` | `30 minutes` | How much time the lanes show, in ms |
| now | `number` |  | A clock you control, e.g. a faster one for a demo. Without it the lanes follow real time, every second |
| onApprove / onReject | `(task: LaneTask) => void` |  | Approve or Reject on a waiting task. Without handlers the lanes change the status themselves |
| onOpen | `(task: LaneTask) => void` |  | Shows an Open link in the tooltip of a block that doesn't wait |
| title | `string` | `"Agents"` | Heading in the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves from block to block, lane by lane
- Enter: Opens a block's tooltip (what got done), or the decision on a waiting one
- Esc: Closes the decision and returns to its block

### Accessibility

- Every lane is a list labelled with the agent's name; every block is a button that names the agent, task, state and time
- A waiting block controls its decision popover (aria-expanded), which is a labelled dialog with Approve focused
- How many tasks need someone is announced politely when it changes

### Motion

- The window slides with the clock: blocks and hand-off curves are drawn from the same time, so they move together; at the left edge blocks slide out and fade
- Running blocks shimmer, a live hand-off curve flows towards the next agent, waiting flags pulse
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything stays still and only updates

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 760px
- Below 520px the names column shrinks to the avatars
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component draws what it gets – update tasks from your agent events (status, end) and the lanes follow
- Give a waiting task an ask (one sentence on what needs deciding); it shows above Approve / Reject
- Give any task a summary – two or three short points on what got done – for the dark tooltip a click opens
- tools takes up to three small logos (React nodes) of the apps a task works in; they sit on white tiles before the title
- Use handoffTo on the task that hands over, pointing at the id of the next agent's task

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-inbox, agent-plan, agent-steering, approval-card

## Agent Plan (Pro)

An agent's step-by-step plan to review before it runs – rename, drag to reorder, remove or add steps, then watch each one run with live timers and retry from a failed step

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-plan
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-plan.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-plan`

### When to use

- An agent is about to do several things in a row and people should agree to the plan first
- Long or expensive runs (tool calls, emails, writes) where a wrong order or an extra step costs real time
- Showing the same plan as it executes – which step is running, how long each took, where it failed

### When not to use

- A single action that needs a yes or no – use Approval Card
- Model reasoning without editable steps – use Thinking State
- A user's own onboarding checklist – use Progress Tracker

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { AgentPlan, type PlanStep } from "@/components/ui/agent-plan";

export function PlanReview({ plan }: { plan: PlanStep[] }) {
  const [steps, setSteps] = useState(plan);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<"draft" | "running" | "done">("draft");

  return (
    <AgentPlan
      title="Prepare the Q3 board update"
      estimate="~2 min"
      steps={steps}
      status={status}
      onChange={setSteps}
      onRun={(final) => {
        setStatus("running");
        agent.run(final); // stream step updates back into setSteps
      }}
      onCancel={() => agent.discard()}
      onRetry={(id) => agent.retryFrom(id)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `PlanStep[]` |  | Controlled steps: { id, title, detail?, tool?, status?, duration?, error? }. Pair with onChange |
| defaultSteps | `PlanStep[]` | `[]` | Initial steps when uncontrolled – edits are kept inside the component |
| status | `"draft" \| "running" \| "done"` | `"draft"` | Review and edit, executing, or finished. Editing is only possible in draft |
| onChange | `(steps: PlanStep[]) => void` |  | Every edit during review: rename, remove, reorder, add |
| onRun | `(steps: PlanStep[]) => void` |  | "Run plan" pressed – gets the steps in their final order. Set status to "running" here. Also shows "Run again" on the tray once done |
| onCancel | `() => void` |  | Shows a Cancel button next to Run plan |
| onRetry | `(stepId: string) => void` |  | Shows "Retry from here" under failed steps |
| title | `string` |  | The goal of the plan, shown as the heading and used as the list's label |
| estimate | `string` |  | Estimated run time shown in review, e.g. "~2 min" |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between steps, their remove buttons, the Add step field and the actions
- ↑ / ↓: Moves focus to the previous or next step
- Alt / ↑ / ↓: Moves the focused step up or down
- Enter: Renames the focused step; Enter again saves. In Add step: adds the step at the end and keeps the field ready for the next one
- Esc: Cancels a rename
- Delete: Removes the focused step

### Accessibility

- The steps are an ordered list labelled with the plan's title; each step is focusable in review and describes its shortcuts
- Moves, renames, removals and additions are announced in a polite live region ("Moved 'Draft the board memo' to position 3 of 5")
- While running, each step carries its status as text, the active one has aria-current="step", and finished or failed steps are announced
- The drag grip is pointer-only; Alt+arrow keys do the same from the keyboard
- Icon buttons are labelled, focus rings show on keyboard focus only, and the folded-away Add step is inert while running

### Motion

- Reordering is live: the dragged step follows the pointer, the others slide aside, and everything settles with a FLIP glide – also for keyboard moves and order changes from props
- Removed steps collapse and the list closes the gap; added steps fade up into place
- Numbers in a hairline ring turn into a ray spinner, then into a check on a light gray fill that draws itself; the progress line fills segment by segment
- Add step folds away when the plan starts, and the tray below the card swaps its actions for the run's status – "Running · 2 of 5" with the elapsed time, then "Done in 14s"
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and the spinner stands still

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 460px; titles and details wrap, tool chips stay on one line
- Below 400px the footer hint drops away, below 340px gutters tighten – works down to 320px
- On touch screens the grip and remove button are always visible
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Give every step a stable id – reorder animations, timers and announcements follow the id, not the index
- Leave duration out to have it measured from when a step turned active; pass it when your agent reports its own timing
- On retry, reset the failed step and everything after it to "pending" and keep status "running"
- Run the steps onRun hands you, not the original proposal – the user may have renamed, removed or reordered them

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: progress-tracker, tool-call-card, approval-card, thinking-state

## Agent Steering (Pro)

Steer an agent while it works – queue a note for the next step and watch it glide into the plan when the agent picks it up, or interrupt right away

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-steering
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-steering.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-steering`

### When to use

- An agent runs for a while and people notice something it should do differently – without stopping it
- Long runs where a correction is cheaper at the next step than a restart from scratch
- Showing which instruction changed which step, so the run stays easy to follow later

### When not to use

- Reviewing a plan before the run starts – use Agent Plan
- Many background runs at a glance – use Agent Inbox
- A single yes or no before the agent acts – use Approval Card

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { AgentSteering, type SteerNote, type SteerStep } from "@/components/ui/agent-steering";

export function Run({ run }: { run: AgentRun }) {
  const [steps, setSteps] = useState<SteerStep[]>(run.steps);
  const [queue, setQueue] = useState<SteerNote[]>([]);

  // Your agent takes the queue in at the start of each step: move the notes into that step – the glide is automatic
  run.on("step", (index) => {
    setSteps((list) => list.map((s, i) => (i === index ? { ...s, status: "active", notes: queue.map((n) => ({ ...n, picked: "next" })) } : s)));
    setQueue([]);
  });

  return (
    <AgentSteering
      title="Migrate users table"
      agent="Opus 5.5"
      steps={steps}
      queue={queue}
      startedAt={run.startedAt}
      onQueue={(text) => setQueue((q) => [...q, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), text }])}
      onInterrupt={(text, id) => run.interrupt(text, id)}
      onRemove={(id) => setQueue((q) => q.filter((n) => n.id !== id))}
      onPause={() => run.pause()}
      onResume={() => run.resume()}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | What the agent is working on, shown as the heading |
| agent | `string` |  | Name of the agent or model, shown under the title |
| steps | `SteerStep[]` |  | The plan: { id, title, status?, duration?, startedAt?, notes? }. status is "done", "active" or "pending" |
| queue | `SteerNote[]` |  | Notes waiting for the next step: { id, text }. Move one into a step's notes (same id, picked set) and it glides over |
| status | `"running" \| "paused" \| "done"` | `"running"` | The run. Clocks tick while running; when done the field closes |
| startedAt | `number \| Date` |  | When the run started – the header clock ticks from here |
| onQueue | `(text: string) => void` |  | ↵ in the field: add the note to your queue |
| onInterrupt | `(text: string, queuedId?: string) => void` |  | ⌘↵ (Ctrl ↵) in the field, or "Now" on a queued note. Shows the shortcut hint and the Now buttons |
| onRemove | `(id: string) => void` |  | ✕ on a queued note |
| onPause / onResume | `() => void` |  | Shows Pause while running and Resume while paused |
| draft / onDraftChange | `string / (text: string) => void` |  | Controlled field text, e.g. to prefill a suggestion |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Steer the agent…"` | Text in the empty field |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↵: Queues the note for the next step
- ⌘ / ↵: Applies the note to the active step right away (Ctrl ↵ on Windows)
- Shift / ↵: New line in the note
- Esc: Clears the field
- Tab: Moves to Pause, the queued notes' Now and ✕ buttons and the send button

### Accessibility

- The plan is an ordered list labelled "Plan"; the active step has aria-current="step"
- Queuing, interrupting and every note the agent picks up are announced in a polite live region
- The field is labelled "Steer the agent" and described by the shortcut hint below it
- Icon buttons have labels: Pause, Resume, Remove “…”, Queue for the next step

### Motion

- A note the agent takes in glides from the queue into its step (620 ms) and lights up softly once it lands
- The card's height follows its content, so the queue opening and closing never jumps
- The active step spins and shimmers; done steps pop their check in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and the shimmer stops

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 460px
- Below 380px the padding gets tighter
- Touch screens get larger buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component never runs anything itself: it shows steps and queue as passed and reports onQueue / onInterrupt / onRemove
- To show that the agent took a note in, remove it from queue and add it (same id, picked: "next" or "now") to the step's notes in one update
- Give each step a startedAt when it becomes active, so its clock is right after re-renders

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-plan, agent-inbox, tool-call-card, thinking-state

## Agent Tree (Pro)

Who started whom – an orchestrator and its sub-agents as a live tree, with status, cost and time on every card, costs rolling up each branch, and branches that fold to one line

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/agent-tree
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-tree.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-tree`

### When to use

- Multi-agent runs where an orchestrator hands parts of a job to sub-agents – and those start their own
- Seeing at a glance which branch is still running, which one waits for you and which one is expensive
- A run overview next to a chat or a log – click a card to open what that agent did

### When not to use

- When things happened, in time order – use Agent Lanes
- One agent's steps – use Agent Plan or Agent Steering
- Handing tasks to agents yourself – use Delegate Board

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentTree, type TreeAgent } from "@/components/ui/agent-tree";

const run: TreeAgent = {
  id: "lead", name: "Orchestrator", model: "Opus 5.5", task: "Launch the new pricing page",
  status: "running", cost: 0.42, started: Date.now() - 80_000,
  children: [
    { id: "research", name: "Researcher", task: "Compare five competitors", status: "done", cost: 0.29, started: Date.now() - 70_000, ended: Date.now() - 25_000 },
    { id: "build", name: "Coder", task: "Build the page", status: "running", cost: 0.18, started: Date.now() - 60_000 },
  ],
};

export function Run() {
  return <AgentTree root={run} onSelect={(agent) => openLog(agent.id)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| root | `TreeAgent` |  | { id, name, task, model?, avatar?, tools?, status, ask?, error?, cost?, started?, ended?, children? } – the whole tree, rebuilt as the run goes on; tools are small marks shown as overlapping tiles before the task |
| status | `"queued" \| "running" \| "waiting" \| "done" \| "failed" \| "stopped"` |  | Per agent – "waiting" reads "Needs you"; queued and stopped agents and their connectors are muted |
| cost | `number` |  | Per agent, its own cost – a card with children shows the whole branch |
| collapsed / defaultCollapsed | `string[]` | `[]` | Ids of folded branches, controlled or uncontrolled |
| onCollapsedChange | `(collapsed: string[]) => void` |  | A branch was folded or opened |
| ask / error | `string` |  | Per agent – what a waiting agent needs you to decide, and what went wrong for a failed one; shown in the window behind "needs you" and "failed" |
| onResolve | `(agent, action: "approve" \| "reject" \| "retry" \| "dismiss") => void` |  | An answer from that window – update the agent's status in your data |
| onSelect | `(agent: TreeAgent) => void` |  | A click on a card – makes the cards clickable |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for running times – without it the tree ticks every second while an agent runs |
| formatCost | `(amount: number) => string` | `dollars, e.g. "$0.42"` | Formats every cost |
| title | `string` | `"Agents"` | Heading of the bar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between the fold buttons – and the cards, when onSelect is set
- Enter: On a card: selects it (onSelect)
- Enter / Space: Folds or opens the focused branch

### Accessibility

- The tree is a tree with groups; every agent is a treeitem labelled with its name and status, aria-expanded on branches
- Fold buttons name what they do, e.g. "Show 2 sub-agents of Researcher"
- "needs you" and "failed" are buttons with aria-expanded; their window is a dialog, the first answer is focused and Esc closes it
- The totals in the bar – agents, running, needs you, failed, cost – are announced politely when they change

### Motion

- A new agent's connector draws itself from the parent's dot, then the card rises in; several new agents rise one after another
- When the tree changes, every card glides to its new place and the connectors follow frame by frame
- Agents that leave – a folded branch, removed data – fade out a beat apart, bottom first, while their connectors pull back into the parent
- Status glyphs: a spinning loader while running, a check when done, a warning triangle when failed, a clock when it needs you
- Costs that still climb – a running agent, a branch with one, the total – carry a light shimmer that runs over the amount
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears at once

### Responsive

- From 560px the first level sits side by side under the root, deeper levels hang below their parent – every card has the same width
- Narrower, every level is indented under its parent and the connectors run down the left; the cards shrink together so the deepest level still fits
- The connectors are measured from the cards, so any width or zoom works
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Pass the whole tree every time something changes – ids keep the cards in place, new ids grow in with a drawn connector
- cost is the agent's own spend; the component adds the children up, so don't pre-sum it
- A failed agent that gets retried is a new child with its own id – keep the failed one, it tells the story
- The connector color is --ui-agt-link (#82bcff), the soft blue of the Project Flow illustration
- The chevron is Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: agent-lanes, agent-plan, delegate-board, agent-steering

## AI Answer (Pro)

Streamed answer with source cards, citation chips that preview their source, copy, regenerate, feedback and follow-ups

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/ai-answer
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/ai-answer.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/ai-answer`

### When to use

- Answers from an assistant that searched your docs, the web or connected tools and should show where each claim comes from
- Research, support or knowledge-base products where people need to check the source before they act

### When not to use

- Casual chat without sources – a plain message bubble is lighter
- Long documents or code – the answer is made for a few paragraphs and lists

### Usage

```tsx
import { AIAnswer, type AnswerSource } from "@/components/ui/ai-answer";

const sources: AnswerSource[] = [
  { name: "Notion", title: "Offsite plan – shortlist and budget", href: "https://notion.so/…", snippet: "Budget €4,500 for three nights…" },
  { name: "Slack", title: "#team-offsite – who can make which dates", href: "https://slack.com/…" },
];

export function Answer({ text, done }: { text: string; done: boolean }) {
  return (
    <AIAnswer
      question="Where should we hold the team offsite?"
      sources={sources}
      // Blank lines: paragraphs · "- ": list · **bold** · [1] or [1,2]: citations (1-based)
      answer={text}
      streaming={!done}
      onRegenerate={() => regenerate()}
      onFeedback={(value, reason) => track("answer_feedback", { value, reason })}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| question | `string` |  | Shown as the title above the sources |
| sources | `AnswerSource[]` |  | Each { title, name, href?, icon?, snippet? }; name is the short label on the citation chip |
| answer | `string` |  | Blank lines make paragraphs, lines starting with "- " a list, **bold**, [1] or [1,3] cite sources (1-based). It may grow while streaming; a different text starts over |
| streaming | `boolean` | `false` | More text is still coming from your model – keeps the cursor going once it has caught up |
| animate | `boolean` | `true` | Stream the text in; false shows it at once |
| speed | `number` | `38` | Words per second while streaming in |
| followUps | `string[]` |  | Related questions shown below the finished answer |
| onFollowUp | `(question: string) => void` |  | A follow-up was clicked |
| onRegenerate | `() => void` |  | Regenerate was clicked – the answer streams in again; pass a new answer to replace it |
| onStop | `() => void` |  | Stop was clicked while writing – cancel your request here |
| onFeedback | `(value: "up" \| "down", reason?: string) => void` |  | Thumbs up, or thumbs down with the reason that was picked |
| feedbackReasons | `string[]` | `["Not accurate", "Wrong source", "Too long", "Out of date"]` | Reasons offered after a thumbs down |
| onCopy | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called with the copied text: the answer without markup plus a numbered source list |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through source cards, citation chips, follow-ups and actions
- Esc: Closes the source preview of the focused chip

### Accessibility

- Citation chips are buttons named after their sources; the preview is a tooltip linked to the chip
- The answer is marked busy while it streams, so screen readers read it once it's complete
- Copy, feedback and status changes are announced in a polite live region

### Motion

- Source cards pop in one after another while the label reads "Reading 6 sources"
- Words fade in out of a light blur, citation chips pop in, a pulsing dot marks where the text grows
- Hovering a chip lights up its source card, hovering a card lights up its chips
- The card glides to its new height; with prefers-reduced-motion the answer appears at once

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 640px; source cards scroll sideways on narrow screens
- Tap a citation chip to open its preview on touch screens
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: thinking-state, chat-composer, comment-thread

---

## Approval Card (Pro)

An agent asks before it acts – risk badge, preview, Approve and Deny with shortcuts, a pausing countdown, and a smooth morph into a resolved row

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/approval-card
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/approval-card.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/approval-card`

### When to use

- An agent is about to do something hard to undo – send email, delete files, spend money, deploy – and a person should say yes first
- Human-in-the-loop tool calls in a chat or an agent run log, one card per pending call
- Requests that should expire on their own when nobody answers

### When not to use

- Many pending requests at once that people triage in bulk – use Decision Inbox
- Harmless, reversible actions – just do them and offer undo
- Destructive actions the user triggered themselves – a regular confirm dialog fits better

### Usage

```tsx
import { ApprovalCard } from "@/components/ui/approval-card";

export function SendApproval({ call }: { call: PendingToolCall }) {
  return (
    <ApprovalCard
      title="Send campaign email"
      description="October product update · Newsletter"
      risk="medium"
      details={[
        { label: "To", value: "Customers – EU (42)" },
        { label: "Subject", value: "What's new in October" },
        { label: "Send", value: "Today, 9:00 AM" },
      ]}
      expiresIn={60}
      onApprove={({ always }) => call.approve({ always })} // return the promise – the button shows a spinner
      onDeny={({ reason }) => call.reject(reason)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | The action, e.g. "Send campaign email" – also the card's accessible name |
| description | `ReactNode` |  | One line of context below the title; truncates |
| risk | `"low" \| "medium" \| "high"` |  | Tinted badge in the header (gray, amber, red); leave out to hide it |
| icon | `ReactNode` | `shield` | Icon in the 32px header tile; SVGs get a 16px stroke style |
| details | `{ label: string; value: ReactNode }[]` |  | Key-value rows in the preview panel |
| preview | `ReactNode` |  | Custom content above the details, e.g. recipients or a diff – children work the same |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Used as the preview when preview isn't set |
| status | `"pending" \| "approved" \| "denied"` |  | Controlled status; setting it back to "pending" starts a fresh request |
| defaultStatus | `"pending" \| "approved" \| "denied"` | `"pending"` | Starting status when uncontrolled |
| onApprove | `({ always }) => void \| Promise` |  | Called on Approve or ⌘/Ctrl+Enter. Return a promise to show a spinner and lock the card; a rejection keeps it pending |
| onDeny | `({ reason: "user" \| "timeout" }) => void` |  | Called on Deny, Escape, or when the countdown runs out |
| onEdit | `() => void` |  | Shows an Edit button before Deny |
| expiresIn | `number` |  | Seconds until the request expires; shown as quiet "Expires in 0:42" text in the tray next to the buttons, amber in the last 10 seconds, paused while hovered or focused |
| onExpire | `() => void` |  | Called when the countdown runs out, right before onDeny({ reason: "timeout" }) |
| allowAlways | `boolean` | `true` | Show the "Always allow this action" checkbox |
| alwaysLabel | `string` | `"Always allow this action"` | Label of the checkbox |
| approveLabel | `string` | `"Approve"` | Primary button label |
| denyLabel | `string` | `"Deny"` | Quiet button label |
| editLabel | `string` | `"Edit"` | Edit button label |
| shortcuts | `boolean` | `true` | Show the ⌘↵ / Esc hints on the buttons – the shortcuts work either way |
| label | `ReactNode` |  | Small label on the gray tray above the card, e.g. "Step 4 · gmail.send" |
| actions | `"tray" \| "card"` | `"tray"` | Where the buttons sit: on the gray tray below the card, or inside the white card (handy in narrow side panels next to other cards) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ⌘ / Enter: Approve while focus is anywhere in the card (Ctrl+Enter on Windows and Linux)
- Escape: Deny while focus is in the card
- Tab: Moves through the checkbox, Edit, Deny and Approve

### Accessibility

- role="group" named by the title and described by the description and the countdown
- Real buttons with aria-keyshortcuts; the kbd hints are aria-hidden
- The decision is announced through a polite live region ("Approved: Send campaign email")
- The countdown has a full text description ("Expires in 24 seconds unless approved…") linked via aria-describedby; the visible clock is aria-hidden so it isn't read every second, and it pauses while the card is hovered or focused
- While an approval is processing the card is aria-busy and the buttons are aria-disabled, so focus is never lost
- After a decision focus moves to the resolved row (tabIndex -1) if it was inside the card

### Motion

- On a decision the card and its tray footer fade and blur out, the height glides down to a compact row inside the tray and the check or cross draws itself in
- The countdown text ticks down once per second without animation and turns amber in the last 10 seconds
- Buttons press in slightly; the checkbox tick scales in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and only the spinner keeps turning slowly

### Responsive

- Fills its container; below 400px card width the buttons share a full-width row and the shortcut hints hide
- Below 340px the risk badge drops the word "risk" and the resolved row drops its time
- Titles, descriptions and detail values truncate instead of wrapping; works down to 320px
- Shortcut hints are hidden on touch screens
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Render one card per pending tool call that needs consent; resolve the tool call with the onApprove / onDeny result
- Return the real execution promise from onApprove so the card stays locked until the action has actually started
- Persist { always: true } per tool name and skip the card next time
- Set risk from the action, not the model's confidence: anything external, paid or irreversible is at least medium
- Keep title an imperative verb phrase and put the concrete values (recipients, amount, target) in details

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: tool-call-card, decision-inbox, thinking-state, thinking-loader

## Autonomy Dial (Pro)

How much an agent may do on its own – a three-stop dial, and its real actions gliding between “Runs on its own” and “Asks you first”, with a lock for what always asks

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/autonomy-dial
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/autonomy-dial.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/autonomy-dial`

### When to use

- Settings of an agent product: how much the agent may do without asking
- Onboarding of a new agent, where people decide how much to trust it before the first run
- Anywhere a permission level is abstract – the list shows what the level actually means

### When not to use

- One decision before one action – use Approval Card
- Turning integrations on and off – use Integration Settings
- Many independent permissions with no levels – a plain list of switches is clearer

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { AutonomyDial, type AgentAction, type AutonomyLevel } from "@/components/ui/autonomy-dial";

const actions: AgentAction[] = [
  { id: "read", label: "Read files and docs", detail: "Drive · Notion", risk: "safe" },
  { id: "draft", label: "Draft emails", risk: "safe" },
  { id: "send", label: "Send emails", detail: "To customers", risk: "risky" },
  { id: "delete", label: "Delete files", risk: "destructive" },
  { id: "spend", label: "Spend money", detail: "Up to $500", risk: "destructive" },
];

export function AgentPermissions() {
  const [level, setLevel] = useState<AutonomyLevel>(1);
  const [pinned, setPinned] = useState(["spend"]);
  return (
    <AutonomyDial
      title="Sales agent"
      actions={actions}
      level={level}
      onLevelChange={setLevel}
      pinned={pinned}
      onPinnedChange={setPinned}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| actions | `AgentAction[]` |  | The agent's actions: { id, label, detail?, risk: "safe" | "risky" | "destructive", icon? } |
| level | `0 \| 1 \| 2` |  | Controlled level: 0 Always ask, 1 If risky (safe actions run), 2 Full auto |
| defaultLevel | `0 \| 1 \| 2` | `1` | Starting level when uncontrolled |
| onLevelChange | `(level: AutonomyLevel) => void` |  | Another level was picked |
| pinned | `string[]` |  | Controlled ids of actions that always ask, whatever the level |
| defaultPinned | `string[]` | `[]` | Starting locks when uncontrolled |
| onPinnedChange | `(pinned: string[]) => void` |  | A lock was set or removed |
| title | `string` | `"Agent permissions"` | Heading, e.g. the agent's name |
| subtitle | `string` | `"What it may do without asking you"` | Line under the heading |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: Picks the previous or next level (also ↑ ↓)
- Tab: Moves from the levels to the locks of the actions
- Space: Sets or removes the focused lock

### Accessibility

- The levels are a radio group labelled "Autonomy", described by a sentence on what the chosen level means
- Both groups are labelled sections; every lock is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label naming its action
- Every change is announced politely: the level and how many actions run on their own or ask first

### Motion

- Actions glide to their new group when the level or a lock changes, a beat after each other
- The card's height follows and the counts roll; a raised white pill glides to the chosen level
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 400px
- Below 340px the detail lines are left out and the levels get tighter
- Without hover (touch) the locks are always visible; touch screens get taller rows
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- asksFirst(action, level, pinned) is exported – use the same rule when the agent runs, so the setting and the behaviour never drift apart
- Rule: pinned always asks; level 0 asks for everything; level 1 runs only "safe" actions; level 2 runs everything not pinned
- Only risky and destructive actions carry a small tag right after the name – a warning glyph and the word, as a soft orange or red pill – safe ones stay quiet
- The risk and lock glyphs are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: approval-card, agent-steering, integration-settings, agent-plan

## Billing Schedule (Pro)

Build a billing phase – start date, duration, products with repeats and timing, discount, minimum and live totals

### When to use

- Quoting and contract tools where a phase of billing is put together – set-up fees, licences, support
- Admin screens for subscriptions with one-off and recurring charges, discounts and minimum commitments

### When not to use

- A simple plan picker – use the Pricing Plans block
- Usage-based pricing with tiers per unit – this works with fixed prices per line

### Usage

```tsx
import { BillingSchedule } from "@/components/ui/billing-schedule";

export function NewContract() {
  return (
    <BillingSchedule
      phase="Build-out phase"
      defaultStart="2026-01-01"

    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| phase | `string` | `"Build-out phase"` | Starting phase name – editable in the summary |
| currency | `string` | `"$"` | Currency symbol for prices and totals |
| catalog | `CatalogItem[]` |  | Products under Add product – { name, repeat, price } |
| defaultLines | `ScheduleLine[]` |  | Lines to start with – products, a discount or a minimum |
| defaultStart | `string` | `"2026-01-01"` | Start date as yyyy-mm-dd |
| onChange | `(schedule) => void` |  | Called with { phase, start, duration, lines } after every change |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the phase name, the fields, every line and the buttons
- Enter: Confirms a price; Esc closes an open menu

### Accessibility

- The lines are a table with column headers; every input and select has a label naming its line
- Duration and Add product are buttons that open listboxes; totals are announced politely

### Motion

- New lines slide in and the table glides to its new height; the duration menu and catalog scale in
- The end date in the summary fades when it changes
- With prefers-reduced-motion changes happen instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 560px; on narrow screens the fields stack and the Repeats column hides
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

- React 19

## Breakdown Chart (Pro)

Stacked bar chart with measure, slice and segment pickers, a hover breakdown and a linked table

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/breakdown-chart
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/breakdown-chart.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/breakdown-chart`

### When to use

- Showing how a set of records splits up – tasks by status and priority, tickets by team, orders by region
- Reports where people want to switch the view themselves without leaving the page

### When not to use

- Values over time – use the KPI Chart
- More than about twelve bars or eight segments – the bars and the legend get hard to read

### Usage

```tsx
import { BreakdownChart } from "@/components/ui/breakdown-chart";

const dimensions = [
  { key: "status", label: "Status", values: ["Todo", "In progress", "Done"] },
  { key: "priority", label: "Priority", values: ["High", "Medium", "Low"], colors: { High: "#e5484d" } },
];
const measures = [
  { key: "count", label: "Task count", unit: "tasks" },
  { key: "points", label: "Story points", unit: "points", field: "points" },
];

export function Sprint({ tasks }) {
  return <BreakdownChart title="Sprint 24" records={tasks} dimensions={dimensions} measures={measures} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| records | `BreakdownRecord[]` |  | Flat records – one per task, ticket or order – with a field per dimension |
| dimensions | `Dimension[]` |  | key, label, values in order, optional colors and icons per value |
| measures | `Measure[]` |  | key, label, unit and the field to sum – without a field records are counted |
| title | `string` | `"Workload"` | Heading in the gray tray |
| defaultMeasure | `string` |  | Measure shown first |
| defaultSlice | `string` |  | Dimension along the bars |
| defaultSegment | `string` |  | Dimension that stacks the bars, or "none" |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the tray |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move through the pickers, the bars and the legend
- ↑ / ↓: Move through an open picker
- Escape: Close a picker

### Accessibility

- Each bar is a button that reads its slice and total; focusing it shows the breakdown
- The table repeats every number, so nothing depends on color or hover
- Legend entries are toggle buttons with a pressed state

### Motion

- Bars grow and re-stack smoothly when the measure, slice or segment changes
- Hovering dims the other bars and highlights the matching table row; reduced motion turns transitions off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: kpi-chart, data-table, change-summary

## Button (Free)

Primary, secondary, ghost and destructive buttons with icons, sizes and a shimmering loading state

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/button
- Section: Components · Buttons
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/button.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/button`

### When to use

- Any action a user triggers: submit a form, send a message, open a dialog
- Async actions that take a moment – the loading state keeps the label readable while it works

### When not to use

- Navigation to another page – use a link so it can be opened in a new tab
- Switching between views – a segmented control or tabs show the current state

### Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";

export function Actions() {
  return (
    <>
      <Button variant="ghost">Cancel</Button>
      <Button>Save changes</Button>
    </>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| variant | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "ghost" \| "destructive"` | `"primary"` | Dark filled, white with an outline, text only, or red for deleting |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 32, 40 or 48px high |
| loading | `boolean` | `false` | Swaps the left icon for a spinner, shimmers the label, sets aria-busy and ignores clicks |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Icon before the label; without children the button becomes square |
| iconRight | `ReactNode` |  | Icon after the label |
| ...props | `button attributes` |  | Everything a native button takes, including ref, type and disabled |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: Activate the button

### Accessibility

- A native button element, so focus, keyboard and form submission work as expected
- While loading it stays focusable and announces aria-busy instead of becoming disabled
- Icon-only buttons need an aria-label – the icon itself is hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- Pressing scales the button to 97%
- Loading swaps the left icon for a spinner and sweeps a band across the label
- When label or icon change, the width glides to the new size and the new content fades in from a soft blur
- With prefers-reduced-motion the sweep stops and changes are instant

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: chat-composer

## Chat Composer (Pro)

Prompt composer with model picker, voice input, app connections and approval request

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/chat-composer
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/chat-composer.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/chat-composer`

### When to use

- The main input of an AI assistant or agent that can act on connected tools
- Flows where the user has to grant extra permissions before a run

### When not to use

- Plain chat between people – a simple text field with a send button is enough
- Very narrow spaces below ~280px, where the toolbar labels get too small

### Usage

```tsx
import { ChatComposer } from "@/components/ui/chat-composer";

export function Assistant() {
  return <ChatComposer onSend={(message) => console.log(message)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Start by typing..."` | Placeholder of the message field |
| models | `ChatModel[]` | `defaultModels` | Entries of the model picker (Auto, Claude, ChatGPT); the first is selected |
| loadMs | `number` | `1300` | Duration of the connect and approval loading states |
| dictation | `string` | `"Draft a short update…"` | Demo transcript that appears word by word in gray while recording – replace with real speech-to-text |
| onSend | `(message: string, details: { model: string }) => void` |  | Called on send or Enter |
| onModelChange | `(model: ChatModel) => void` |  | Called when a model is picked |
| onAttach | `() => void` |  | Called when the plus button is clicked – open your own picker here |
| onConnectApps | `() => void` |  | Called when “Connect apps” is clicked |
| onRequestApproval | `() => void` |  | Called when “Request approval” is clicked |
| onSelectProject | `() => void` |  | Called when “Select a project” is clicked |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Send the message
- Shift + Enter: New line
- ↑ / ↓: Open the model picker and move through it
- Home / End: Jump to the first or last model
- Enter / Space: Pick the highlighted model (in the picker)
- Esc: Close the model picker or discard a recording

### Accessibility

- Loading and result states are announced through a polite live region
- Busy buttons expose aria-busy; the hidden tray row is inert and aria-hidden
- Clicking anywhere on the white card focuses the message field
- The model picker is a listbox with aria-activedescendant, so screen readers follow the highlight

### Motion

- Connecting apps runs two shimmer sweeps while the logos hop, then the card slides down to reveal “Select a project”
- Requesting approval waves the hand, then morphs into the “Unrestricted access” pill
- The model picker morphs out of the corner next to its button, opens toward the side with more room and stays inside the visible frame
- A hover fill fades in under the pointer and glides between rows
- While recording, the heard words appear in gray and turn dark once confirmed; a dotted audio trace scrolls next to the controls
- All transitions collapse to instant changes with prefers-reduced-motion

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 680px wide; all sizes follow the width via container query units and stop growing at a compact maximum
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Cited Answer (Pro)

An AI answer wired to its sources – point at a citation to light up its sentence and source, click to unfold the quoted passage with the matching words marked

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/cited-answer
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/cited-answer.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/cited-answer`

### When to use

- Search, research and support answers where people need to check which sentence comes from which source before they trust it
- A finished answer from your RAG pipeline that already knows the passage behind each claim – the preview shows exactly that passage
- Next to AI Answer: use this one once the answer is done and the point is checking it, not watching it stream

### When not to use

- Answers that are still streaming, with follow-ups and feedback – use AI Answer
- Casual chat without sources – a plain message is lighter
- Long reports with dozens of sources – the tray is made for a handful of chips

### Usage

```tsx
import { CitedAnswer, type CitedSegment, type CitedSource } from "@/components/ui/cited-answer";

const sources: CitedSource[] = [
  {
    id: "caching",
    site: "Tokenwise",
    title: "Prompt caching, explained",
    url: "https://tokenwise.dev/blog/prompt-caching",
    date: "Sep 18, 2026",
    quote: "A cached prefix is read instead of recomputed …",
    highlight: ["read instead of recomputed"],
  },
];

const segments: CitedSegment[] = [
  { text: "Prompt caching reuses the processed start of your prompt.", cite: ["caching"] },
  { text: " Streaming makes the rest feel faster." },
];

export function Answer() {
  return <CitedAnswer segments={segments} sources={sources} pagesRead={12} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| segments | `CitedSegment[]` |  | { text, cite?, paragraph? } – the answer in order. cite lists source ids (one marker each); paragraph starts a new paragraph. Spaces at the edges of text stay outside the highlight |
| sources | `CitedSource[]` |  | { id, title, site, url?, date?, quote?, highlight?, icon? } – numbered in this order, one chip each |
| pagesRead | `number` |  | Pages read while searching – shown in the head as "3 sources · 12 pages read" |
| defaultOpen | `string` |  | Id of the source whose preview is open at first |
| onOpenSource | `(source: CitedSource) => void` |  | Called by Open source. With it the link doesn't navigate on its own; without it the url opens in a new tab |
| onPreviewChange | `(id: string \| null) => void` |  | Called when a preview opens, switches or closes |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | A button on the tray, e.g. Follow up |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the citation markers in reading order, the preview's buttons, the source chips and the action
- Enter / Space: Opens or closes the preview of a marker or chip
- ← / → / Home / End: Move between the source chips
- Esc: Closes the preview and puts focus on its chip

### Accessibility

- Markers and chips are buttons named "Source 2: Latency Notes – title", with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the preview
- Focusing a marker or chip lights up the same sentences and chip as hovering does
- The preview is a named region; while closed it is inert
- The line on the tray is announced politely – what you point at, and "Quote copied"

### Motion

- Hovering a marker gives its sentence a soft tint and lights up its chip; hovering a chip tints every sentence that cites it and fades the rest of the answer
- The preview unfolds below the answer and folds away again; switching to another source crossfades its content in place
- The tray line crossfades: the old line fades out underneath while the new one fades in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 460px and works from 300px. Chips wrap onto a second row and long names shorten; below 360px the card gets tighter and the preview drops its number tag, below 280px Copy quote keeps only its icon
- Touch screens: larger hit areas around the markers and taller chips and buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Numbers come from the order of sources, not from the text – cite by id, and reorder sources to renumber
- The last word of a cited sentence stays on the line with its markers, so a marker never starts a line on its own
- Ids in cite that aren't in sources are skipped, so a hallucinated citation never shows a broken marker
- Without highlight, words of five letters or more (and numbers) that the quote shares with its citing sentences are marked – pass highlight for exact phrases
- The component doesn't fetch pages – quote should be the passage your retrieval step actually used

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: ai-answer, tool-call-card, thinking-state

---

## Combobox (Pro)

Pick one or many from a searchable, grouped list – chips with avatars, highlighted matches, create-on-the-fly and full keyboard support

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/combobox
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/combobox.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/combobox`

### When to use

- Assigning people, labels, tags or projects – anything picked from a list that's too long to scan
- Filters where several values can apply at once, like owners or statuses
- Tag fields that should also accept new values (creatable)

### When not to use

- Up to five fixed choices – checkboxes or a segmented control show them all at once
- Free text with no list behind it – use a plain input
- Running actions rather than picking values – use the command menu

### Usage

```tsx
import { Combobox, type ComboboxOption } from "@/components/ui/combobox";

const people: ComboboxOption[] = [
  { value: "maya", label: "Maya Chen", hint: "Product Designer", avatar: true, group: "Design" },
  { value: "sara", label: "Sara Okafor", hint: "Staff Engineer", avatar: "/avatars/sara.jpg", group: "Engineering" },
  { value: "elif", label: "Elif Yilmaz", hint: "Head of Product", avatar: true, group: "Product" },
];

export function Reviewers() {
  const [reviewers, setReviewers] = useState<string[]>(["maya"]);
  return (
    <Combobox
      label="Reviewers"
      options={people}
      value={reviewers}
      onChange={setReviewers}
      placeholder="Add reviewers…"
      maxVisibleTags={4}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options | `{ value, label, hint?, avatar?, color?, icon?, group?, keywords? }[]` |  | The list. avatar is an image URL or true for initials; options with the same group are listed under one title |
| multiple | `boolean` | `true` | Pick many (chips) or one – one closes the list after picking |
| value | `string[]` |  | Controlled values (also for single choice, with at most one entry) |
| defaultValue | `string[]` | `[]` | Starting values when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(value: string[], options: ComboboxOption[]) => void` |  | Called on every pick, removal or creation |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Search…"` | Shown while nothing is picked |
| creatable | `boolean` | `false` | Offer a create row when no option matches the typed text exactly |
| onCreate | `(text: string) => ComboboxOption \| void` |  | Builds the new option – defaults to { value: text, label: text } |
| createLabel | `(text: string) => string` | `Create “…”` | Text of the create row, e.g. Invite “…” |
| maxVisibleTags | `number` |  | Show at most this many chips, the rest as a "+3" chip |
| label | `string` |  | Visible label above the field (also names the list) |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Open the list right away |
| emptyText | `string` | `"No results"` | Shown when nothing matches |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Open the list, then move between rows
- ↵: Pick or unpick the active row (or create)
- ⌫: In the empty field: highlight the last chip, press again to remove it
- Esc: Close the list; when closed, clear the typed text
- Tab: Close the list and move on

### Accessibility

- Follows the ARIA combobox pattern: the input has role combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant; the list is a listbox with grouped options
- Picked rows carry aria-selected, the listbox is aria-multiselectable in multiple mode
- Picks and removals are announced in a polite live region, together with the count
- Focus stays in the input while clicking rows and chip × buttons; the field shows a soft focus ring

### Motion

- Chips grow in with a small pop and fold away after a short flash; the field glides to its new height when chips wrap
- A gray highlight glides to the active row; the list glides to its new height while filtering
- Check marks pop in with a gentle spring; the "+3" chip and the count roll up or down
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- The list is as wide as the field, so it always fits the screen
- Chips wrap onto new lines and long names truncate – works down to 320px
- Touch screens get 44px rows, bigger chip buttons and 16px input text (no iOS zoom)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: filter-menu, command-menu, integration-picker

---

## Command Menu (Pro)

Search and run anything from one field – tool actions with logos and ⌘1–⌘5, everyday commands with icons

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/command-menu
- Section: Components · Navigation
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/command-menu.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/command-menu`

### When to use

- A ⌘K menu that runs actions across the tools your product connects to
- Power users who want to reach any page or action without the mouse

### When not to use

- The only way to reach something – keep the main navigation visible as well
- Fewer than five actions – buttons are easier to discover

### Usage

```tsx
import { CommandMenu, type CommandGroup } from "@/components/ui/command-menu";

export function Commands({ onClose }: { onClose: () => void }) {
  return (
    <CommandMenu
      autoFocus
      onClose={onClose}
      onRun={(id, query) => (id === "ask" ? askAssistant(query) : runCommand(id))}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| groups | `CommandGroup[]` | `Suggestions, Share, General, Go to` | Each { id, label, commands: { id, label, hint?, logo? | icon?, keys?, keywords? }[] }; the group with id "suggestions" gets ⌘1–⌘5 |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Type a command or search…"` | Text in the empty field |
| onRun | `(id: string, query?: string) => void` |  | Called when a command runs; the assistant fallback sends "ask" and the typed text |
| onClose | `() => void` |  | Runs on Esc in an empty field – close your dialog here |
| autoFocus | `boolean` |  | Focus the field when the menu appears |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↑ / ↓: Move row by row through all sections
- ↵: Run the highlighted command
- Tab: Jump to the next section (Shift Tab goes back)
- ⌘ / 1–5: Run a suggestion straight away (Ctrl on Windows)
- Esc: Clear the field, then close
- ⌘ / K: Focus the field from anywhere

### Accessibility

- The field is a combobox that controls the list; the highlighted command is the active option
- Groups are labelled, shortcut keys are hidden from screen readers
- What just ran is announced in a polite live region

### Motion

- The gray highlight glides from row to row
- The row that runs gives a short press; a check and its name appear in the tray below
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 600px; on phones shortcut keys and hints are left out
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Comment Thread (Free)

One comment with replies – an assistant reports what it did, folds open details and answers @mentions

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/comment-thread
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/comment-thread.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/comment-thread`

### When to use

- A single conversation attached to a selection, a cell or a line of text
- Showing what an assistant did after someone asked for a change

### When not to use

- A feed of many comments – use the Comments Panel

### Usage

```tsx
import { AssistantMark, CommentThread } from "@/components/ui/comment-thread";

const atlas = { name: "Atlas", avatar: <AssistantMark />, assistant: true };

export function Thread({ messages, me }) {
  return (
    <CommentThread
      messages={messages}
      currentUser={me}
      assistant={atlas}
      onReply={async (text) => (text.includes("@Atlas") ? await api.ask(text) : undefined)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| messages | `ThreadMessage[]` |  | id, author, createdAt, text – assistant replies can add a status line with folding details |
| currentUser | `ThreadAuthor` |  | Author of new replies |
| assistant | `ThreadAuthor` |  | Shown with a thinking state while an answer is on its way |
| onReply | `(text) => ThreadMessage \| Promise<ThreadMessage \| void> \| void` |  | Return a message (or a promise) for the assistant to answer, nothing to just post |
| onClose | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button |
| title | `string` | `"Comment"` | Heading in the gray tray |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Send the reply
- Tab: Reach the status lines to fold their details open

### Accessibility

- Status lines are buttons with aria-expanded; folded details are inert
- The thread announces new replies politely

### Motion

- Replies fade in, the thinking text shimmers, details fold open – reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: comments-panel, chat-composer

## Comments Panel (Pro)

Comment feed with filters, runnable /edit commands, resolve and a composer

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/comments-panel
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/comments-panel.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/comments-panel`

### When to use

- A comments sidebar next to a document, design or record
- Collaboration with an assistant that can apply edits people suggest with /edit

### When not to use

- Long discussions with nested replies – use the Comment Thread for one conversation

### Usage

```tsx
import { CommentsPanel } from "@/components/ui/comments-panel";

export function Sidebar({ comments, me }) {
  return (
    <CommentsPanel
      comments={comments}
      currentUser={me}
      onRunEdit={(c) => api.applyEdit(c.text)}
      onAdd={(c) => api.saveComment(c)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| comments | `PanelComment[]` |  | id, author ({ name, avatar }), createdAt and text – text starting with /edit becomes a runnable edit |
| currentUser | `CommentAuthor` |  | Author of new comments |
| onRunEdit | `(comment) => Promise<void> \| void` |  | Runs an edit; the button shows Running… until the promise settles |
| onAdd | `(comment) => void` |  | Called with every new comment |
| onClose | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button |
| title | `string` | `"Comments"` | Heading in the gray tray |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move through tabs, sort, comments and the composer
- Enter: Send the comment in the composer

### Accessibility

- Filters are tabs, sorting is a menu of radio items, resolve is a toggle button
- Times are real time elements; the list announces new comments politely

### Motion

- New comments fade in, edits show a spinner, the sort menu drops in – reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: comment-thread, smart-recommendation
