## OTP Input (Free)

The verification code field done right – a gliding focus ring, paste and SMS autofill, a calm shake on errors and a morph into Verified

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/otp-input
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/otp-input.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/otp-input`

### When to use

- Two-step sign-in, email or phone verification, confirming a sensitive action with a one-time code
- Any short code people copy from an email or SMS – paste and autofill fill every box at once

### When not to use

- Codes longer than about 8 characters or with free-form text – a plain text field is easier to read and correct
- Passwords or PINs that must stay hidden – the boxes show what's typed

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { OtpInput, type OtpStatus } from "@/components/ui/otp-input";

export function VerifyEmail() {
  const [code, setCode] = useState("");
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<OtpStatus>("idle");
  const [triesLeft, setTriesLeft] = useState(3);

  async function verify(value: string) {
    setStatus("verifying");
    const res = await fetch("/api/verify", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ code: value }) });
    if (res.ok) {
      setStatus("success");
      router.push("/dashboard");
    } else {
      setTriesLeft((n) => n - 1);
      setStatus("error");
    }
  }

  return (
    <OtpInput
      value={code}
      onChange={(next) => {
        setCode(next);
        if (status === "error" && next) setStatus("idle");
      }}
      onComplete={verify}
      status={status}
      errorMessage={`That code didn't work. ${triesLeft} tries left.`}
      separator
      autoFocus
      onResend={() => fetch("/api/send-code", { method: "POST" })}
      resendIn={30}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| length | `number` | `6` | Number of boxes |
| separator | `boolean \| number` | `false` | A small dash between the boxes – true puts it in the middle, a number after that many boxes |
| numeric | `boolean` | `true` | Digits only with the numeric keyboard on phones; false allows letters too, shown in capitals |
| value | `string` |  | The code – makes the field controlled |
| defaultValue | `string` | `""` | Starting code when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(code: string) => void` |  | Every change: typing, Backspace, paste, autofill and the clearing after an error |
| onComplete | `(code: string) => void` |  | Called once the last box is filled by the user – the place to start verifying |
| status | `"idle" \| "verifying" \| "error" \| "success"` | `"idle"` | Verifying shimmers and locks the field, error shakes and shows the message, success morphs into the pill |
| errorMessage | `ReactNode` | `"That code didn't work. Try again."` | Shown below the boxes after an error, until the user types again |
| clearOnError | `boolean` | `true` | Clears the boxes shortly after the shake, ready for the next try |
| successLabel | `string` | `"Verified"` | Text in the pill on success |
| onResend | `() => void` |  | Shows "Didn't get a code?" below the boxes with a countdown that becomes a Resend button; clicking restarts the countdown |
| resendIn | `number` | `30` | Seconds until the code can be resent |
| align | `"start" \| "center"` | `"start"` | Where the boxes and the lines below them sit |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Dims the field and ignores input |
| autoFocus | `boolean` | `false` | Focuses the field on mount (without scrolling) |
| label | `string` | `"Verification code"` | Accessible name; the number of digits is added |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- 0–9: Fills the active box and moves on; typing on a filled box replaces it
- ⌫: Clears the box and goes back one
- ← / →: Moves between the filled boxes and the next empty one
- Home / End: Jumps to the first box, or to the next empty one
- ⌘ / V: Pastes a whole code – spaces and dashes are ignored

### Accessibility

- One real text input carries the whole code, so screen readers hear one field ("Verification code, 6 digits") instead of six
- autocomplete="one-time-code" lets iOS and Android offer the code from an SMS; inputMode="numeric" opens the number pad
- Errors set aria-invalid and point to the message with aria-describedby; verifying, errors, success and resend are announced in a polite live region

### Motion

- A single focus ring glides from box to box with a softly blinking caret; digits pop in out of a short blur
- Pasted or autofilled codes fill the boxes one after another
- Verifying: a soft light passes over the boxes. Error: a calm shake, red borders, the message grows in below and the code fades out for the next try
- Success: the boxes slide together while one frame morphs its width into a "Verified" pill and the check draws in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Container query: the boxes shrink to fit their container – six boxes with a separator fit a 320px phone
- Inputs use 16px text under the hood, so iOS doesn't zoom in on focus
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: combobox, segmented-control, button, toaster

---

## Permission Request (Pro)

An agent asks for one specific right – who, why and exactly what will happen – and you allow it once, for an hour or always; then it folds into one line with the time left and Revoke

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/permission-request
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/permission-request.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/permission-request`

### When to use

- An agent hits an action it isn't allowed to do yet and asks for that one right – push to main, send emails, spend money
- Granting access for a while instead of forever: just once, for an hour, or always
- Anywhere people should see exactly what will happen – the files, recipients or amounts – before they say yes

### When not to use

- Setting up front how much an agent may do in general – use Autonomy Dial
- Reviewing a finished result before it goes out – use Approval Card or Agent Inbox
- Connecting a tool for the first time (OAuth) – that's the provider's consent screen

### Usage

```tsx
import { PermissionRequest } from "@/components/ui/permission-request";

export function PushRequest({ onAnswer }: { onAnswer: (allowed: boolean, until?: number) => void }) {
  return (
    <PermissionRequest
      agent={{ name: "Coder", model: "GPT-6 Sol" }}
      action="push to main"
      target="acme/web"
      risk="risky"
      reason="The fix for the flaky checkout test passed review and all checks."
      preview={[
        { id: "a", label: "src/checkout/cart.ts", meta: "+12 −4" },
        { id: "b", label: "Deploys to production after the merge" },
      ]}
      onDecisionChange={(d) => d && onAnswer(d.allow, d.until)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| agent | `{ name, model?, avatar? }` |  | Who asks – the avatar is a small mark, e.g. the model maker's logo; defaults to initials |
| action | `string` |  | What it wants to do, read after "wants to", e.g. "push to main" |
| target | `string` |  | Where, e.g. "acme/web" or "Stripe · live mode" – shown under the title with toolIcon |
| toolIcon | `ReactNode` |  | The tool's mark next to the target |
| risk | `"safe" \| "risky" \| "destructive"` | `"risky"` | Risky and destructive carry a tag; destructive also turns Allow red and leaves out Always |
| reason | `string` |  | The agent's own words on why it needs this |
| preview | `{ id, label, meta?, icon? }[]` |  | Exactly what will happen – files, recipients, amounts; meta is right-aligned, e.g. "+12 −4" |
| previewTitle | `string` | `"What will happen"` | Heading of the preview |
| previewLimit | `number` | `3` | Rows shown before "N more" |
| scopes | `("once" \| "timed" \| "always")[]` | `all three` | The choices of how long; one choice hides the switch |
| scope / defaultScope / onScopeChange | `PermissionScope` | `"once"` | Controlled or uncontrolled choice of how long |
| duration | `number` | `60` | Minutes a timed grant holds |
| decision / defaultDecision | `PermissionDecision \| null` |  | { allow, scope, at, until? } – null while it waits |
| onDecisionChange | `(decision \| null) => void` |  | Allow, Deny – and null for Revoke, Change or Ask again |
| now | `number` | `Date.now()` | The clock for the time left – without it the card ticks every second while a timed grant runs |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Allows, with the chosen scope – while the focus is in the card
- Esc: Denies
- ← / →: Picks how long

### Accessibility

- While it waits the card is a dialog labelled by its title ("Coder wants to push to main") and described by the reason
- How long is a radio group; the Allow button names the choice, e.g. "Allow for 1 hour"
- The decided line is a status, so screen readers announce "Allowed for 1 hour" or "Denied"

### Motion

- The preview rows rise in a beat after each other; the Allow label swaps softly when the scope changes
- On a decision the card folds to one line, the check or cross pops in, and a thin bar drains until a timed grant runs out
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 400px
- Below 340px the reason loses its indent, the buttons share the width and the keyboard hints go
- Touch screens get taller choices and buttons and no keyboard hints
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The component only asks – store the decision and check it where the agent acts: allow, and for scope "timed" also Date.now() < until
- Destructive actions can never be allowed for always – the choice isn't offered, even if scopes lists it
- Revoke, Change and Ask again all call onDecisionChange(null): treat it as "not allowed, ask again"
- Keep the preview concrete (file names, addresses, amounts) – that is what makes people comfortable saying yes
- The icons are Hugeicons Free (MIT) – keep the credit comment when you copy the file

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: autonomy-dial, approval-card, agent-inbox, tool-call-card

---

## Progress Tracker (Free)

Onboarding checklist with an animated progress bar, ticks that draw themselves and auto play

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/progress-tracker
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/progress-tracker.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/progress-tracker`

### When to use

- Onboarding checklists that guide new users through their first steps
- Any short list of tasks where progress should feel rewarding

### When not to use

- Long task lists – past roughly eight steps the card gets hard to scan
- Long step labels – each step stays on one line and cuts off with an ellipsis
- Steps that must happen in a fixed order – use a stepper that locks the next step

### Usage

```tsx
import { ProgressTracker } from "@/components/ui/progress-tracker";

const steps = [
  { id: "tools", label: "Connect your imported tools" },
  { id: "notify", label: "Turn on notifications" },
  { id: "project", label: "Create a project", done: true },
];

export function Onboarding() {
  return <ProgressTracker title="Getting started" steps={steps} onChange={save} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `ProgressStep[]` |  | Each step has an id, a label, an optional done flag and icon |
| title | `string` | `"Getting started"` | Heading above the bar |
| autoPlay | `boolean` | `false` | Ticks the open steps one by one and starts over – stops when someone clicks or types |
| interval | `number` | `2200` | Pause between two automatic steps, in ms |
| onChange | `(steps: ProgressStep[]) => void` |  | Called with every step and its state |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the card |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between the steps
- Space / Enter: Tick or untick the focused step

### Accessibility

- Each step is a checkbox with aria-checked; the bar is a progressbar with the count as text
- Any click or key press stops the automatic play, so it never fights the user

### Motion

- The bar fills smoothly and a light sweeps across it each time a step is done
- The check ring fills and pops, then the tick draws itself
- A line strikes through the label, line by line, while it fades to gray
- On mount the card settles in and the rows fade up one after another
- Steps stay in place so nothing jumps; the counter rolls to the new number
- With prefers-reduced-motion every change is instant

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: button, chat-composer

## Project Card (Pro)

A two-line project summary that quietly unfolds on hover – a progress ring with one segment per subtask, a people filter and a status picker, all linked by hover

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/project-card
- Section: Components · Cards
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/project-card.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/project-card`

### When to use

- Boards, lists and sidebars where many projects or tasks sit next to each other and the details should be one hover away
- Anything with a short summary and a longer truth behind it – a project, a ticket, a deal, an agent run
- When opening a separate page or drawer would be too heavy for a quick look and a small edit

### When not to use

- Long content or forms – open a drawer or a page instead; this card is for a glance and a tick
- Dense tables – a row that grows on hover pushes everything below it around
- When the details must stay visible – show the open card as a static layout instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { ProjectCard } from "@/components/ui/project-card";

export function OnboardingCard() {
  return (
    <ProjectCard
      title="Onboarding flow"
      tasks={[
        { id: "welcome", label: "Welcome screen", done: true, assignee: "Mara" },
        { id: "workspace", label: "Workspace setup", done: true, assignee: "Jonas" },
        { id: "invite", label: "Invite teammates", assignee: "Mara" },
      ]}
      status="progress"
      due="Oct 24"
      members={[{ name: "Mara" }, { name: "Jonas" }]}
      action={{ label: "Open", onClick: () => router.push("/projects/onboarding") }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | Name of the project |
| tasks | `ProjectTask[]` |  | { id, label, done?, assignee? } – one ring segment and one row each; assignee is a member's name |
| onTasksChange | `(tasks: ProjectTask[]) => void` |  | Called with the full list after a tick. With it the card shows exactly what you pass; without it the ticks live inside the card |
| status | `string` | `first option` | Id of the chosen status |
| statuses | `ProjectOption[]` | `To do, In progress, In review, Done` | { id, label, tone? } – tone is red, amber, green, blue, violet or gray and also picks the icon; icon replaces it |
| onStatusChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the picked status |
| due | `string` |  | Ready-to-show due date, e.g. "Oct 24" – shown as "Due Oct 24" |
| members | `ProjectMember[]` |  | { name, avatar? } – the avatars in the head; hovering one shows only that person's subtasks. Initials on a soft color without an image |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | A button on the tray of the open card, e.g. Open |
| hint | `ReactNode` | `"2 left" / "All done"` | The line on the tray while nothing is hovered |
| trigger | `"hover" \| "click"` | `"hover"` | Hover opens under the mouse; taps and the keyboard always toggle |
| open | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Starts open when uncontrolled |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the card opens or closes |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the card: opens or closes it
- Tab: Through the status, the people, the subtasks and the action
- Space: On a subtask: ticks or unticks it. On a person: keeps or releases their filter. On the status: unfolds the options
- Esc: Closes the status options first, then the card

### Accessibility

- The head is one button with aria-expanded whose name carries the summary: title, progress, status and due date
- Subtasks are checkboxes, the people are toggle buttons, the status options are a radio group
- While the card is closed, everything inside is inert – nothing hidden can be focused or read
- Focusing a subtask or a person does what hovering does, and the line on the tray is announced politely

### Motion

- Nothing travels: the head stays where it is and the list unfolds below it while it fades in
- The status options unfold in the same way, in place
- Hovering a subtask thickens its ring segment and brings in the assignee's avatar; ticking fills the circle, draws the check and turns the segment dark
- Hovering a person fades everyone else's subtasks and segments
- The line on the tray swaps with a short rise; the number in the ring pops when it changes
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 320px. Below 290px the date drops its word ("Oct 24") and the avatars move closer; a long title is cut with an ellipsis and nothing runs under the avatars
- Touch screens: a tap opens, a tap outside closes, rows and options are taller and the assignee avatars are always visible
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- The card grows downward when it opens – in a list, give it room or lay it over the next items with position absolute in a fixed-height slot
- A task's assignee must match a member's name exactly – that is what links rows, avatars and the people filter
- More than about twelve subtasks make the ring segments too small to point at – group them first

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: progress-tracker, agent-plan, compact-breakdown

---

## Prompt Library (Pro)

Saved prompt templates with variables – type straight into the sentence, watch the finished prompt assemble below, and use it once every variable is filled

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/prompt-library
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/prompt-library.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/prompt-library`

### When to use

- AI products where people reuse the same prompts with small changes – summaries, release notes, outreach, debugging
- Next to a chat composer, as the place to pick a saved prompt, fill in the blanks and send it
- Team prompt libraries where the template stays fixed and only a few words change per use

### When not to use

- Free writing – a plain composer is faster when nothing repeats
- Long templates with many variables – past about six fields a form with labels reads better than a sentence
- Choosing a command or action – use Command Menu

### Usage

```tsx
import { PromptLibrary } from "@/components/ui/prompt-library";

export function Prompts() {
  return (
    <PromptLibrary
      templates={[
        {
          id: "meeting",
          title: "Summarize a meeting",
          category: "Notes",
          body: "Summarize the meeting below for {audience} in under {length}.",
          variables: { length: { default: "150 words" } },
        },
        {
          id: "error",
          title: "Explain an error",
          category: "Debug",
          body: "Explain this {language} error in plain words: {error}.",
        },
      ]}
      onUse={(prompt) => send(prompt)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| templates | `PromptTemplate[]` |  | { id, title, category?, tone?, body, variables? } – body holds the variables in curly braces, e.g. {audience}; variables maps a name to { description?, default? } |
| value | `string` |  | Id of the chosen template (controlled) |
| defaultValue | `string` |  | Id chosen at first when uncontrolled – the first template by default |
| onSelect | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called when another template is chosen |
| onUse | `(prompt: string, template: PromptTemplate, values: Record<string, string>) => void` |  | Called with the finished prompt when Use is pressed – only possible once every variable is filled |
| onCopy | `(prompt: string) => void` |  | Called after the prompt was copied to the clipboard |
| title | `string` | `"Prompts"` | Heading above the list |
| useLabel | `string` | `"Use prompt"` | Label of the use button |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ↓: From the search field into the list
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: Move through the list – the template opens as you go
- Esc: Clears the search
- Tab: Through the variable fields, then Copy and Use
- Enter: In a variable field: jumps to the next empty one, or uses the prompt once all are filled

### Accessibility

- A group named by the list's title; the templates are a listbox with options and aria-selected, only the chosen one is in the tab order
- Every variable is a real text field labelled with its name and description
- Use stays focusable while not ready (aria-disabled) and the tray says how many variables are missing
- A polite live region announces when all variables are filled, when the prompt was copied and when it was used
- The outgoing template that fades out during a switch is inert and hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The highlight slides along the list to the chosen template while the content crossfades – the old one fades out underneath
- The part you type into lights up in the field and in the preview, then fades back
- The token estimate on the tray rolls to its new value as you type
- Use pulses once when the last variable gets filled; Copy turns into a check for a moment
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 640px. Below 540px the list moves on top of the template; below 360px Copy keeps only its icon
- Fields grow with what you type and never get wider than the line
- Touch screens: taller list rows, fields and buttons
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Variables are written as {name} with letters, digits, - or _; the same name used twice is one field
- Values are kept per template inside the card, so switching back and forth keeps what was typed
- The token number is an estimate (about four characters per token) – pass the prompt to your tokenizer when it has to be exact
- Category colors follow the order the categories appear; set tone on a template to pick one

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: chat-composer, command-menu, writing-assistant

## Reaction Bar (Free)

Like, comment, repost and share in one pill – icons pop and fill, counts roll in digit by digit

```tsx
import { ReactionBar } from "@/components/ui/reaction-bar";

export function PostActions({ post }) {
  return (
    <ReactionBar
      reactions={{ like: { count: post.likes, active: post.liked }, comment: { count: post.comments } }}
      onReact={(key, state) => api.react(post.id, key, state.active)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reactions | `Partial<Record<ReactionKey, { count; active? }>>` |  | Starting count and pressed state per action |
| onReact | `(key, state) => void` |  | Called after a toggle with the new count and state |
| actions | `ReactionKey[]` | `["like", "comment", "repost", "share"]` | Which actions to show, in order |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the pill |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between the actions
- Enter / Space: Toggle the focused action

### Accessibility

- Every action is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label that includes its count
- The rolling digits are decorative – the label carries the number

### Motion

- The icon shrinks, springs and fills with its color; the count glides to its new width and changed digits roll in
- Reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: button, comments-panel

## Segmented Control (Free)

Switch between two to six options – a raised pill or underline that glides, stretches a little and can be dragged across, with icons, counts and badges

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/segmented-control
- Section: Components · Navigation
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/segmented-control.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/segmented-control`

### When to use

- Switching between two to six views of the same content – sections of a dashboard, list / board / calendar, monthly / yearly
- A choice that applies right away and where every option should stay visible

### When not to use

- More than six options or long labels – use a select or a menu
- Choices that are confirmed with a Save button inside a form – radio buttons read clearer there
- Turning one thing on or off – that's a switch

### Usage

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from "@/components/ui/segmented-control";

export function DashboardTabs() {
  const [section, setSection] = useState("overview");
  return (
    <SegmentedControl
      aria-label="Dashboard section"
      kind="tabs"
      value={section}
      onChange={setSection}
      options={[
        { value: "overview", label: "Overview", controls: "panel-overview" },
        { value: "analytics", label: "Analytics", controls: "panel-analytics" },
        { value: "reports", label: "Reports", controls: "panel-reports" },
        { value: "notifications", label: "Notifications", count: unread, controls: "panel-notifications" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| options | `SegmentOption[]` |  | { value, label?, icon?, count?, badge?, disabled?, ariaLabel?, controls? } – two to six work best; give icon-only options an ariaLabel |
| value | `string` |  | Controlled value |
| defaultValue | `string` | `first enabled option` | Starting value when uncontrolled |
| onChange | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the new value – on click, while dragging the pill and on arrow keys |
| size | `"sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | 26, 30 or 36px tall options (40px+ on touch screens) |
| variant | `"tray" \| "underline"` | `"tray"` | A gray track with a raised white pill, or text tabs on a hairline with a sliding line |
| fullWidth | `boolean` | `false` | Fills its container with equal segments, each as wide as the widest one needs |
| kind | `"radio" \| "tabs"` | `"radio"` | A radiogroup, or a tablist that switches panels (pair with controls on each option) |
| disabled | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the whole control |
| aria-label | `string` |  | Names the group – or use aria-labelledby |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Focuses the active option (one tab stop for the whole control)
- ← / →: Moves to and selects the previous or next option, wrapping around; ↑ ↓ too as a radiogroup
- Home / End: Selects the first or last option
- ↵: Selects the focused option (Space works too)

### Accessibility

- A radiogroup with radios (aria-checked), or a tablist with tabs (aria-selected, aria-controls) with kind="tabs"
- Roving tabindex: only the active option is in the tab order; disabled options are skipped by the arrow keys
- The semibold copy of each label is aria-hidden, so names are read once; counts and badges are part of the name
- Visible focus ring on the focused option

### Motion

- The indicator glides to the picked option; the edge facing the target leads, so it stretches a little and settles – calm, no bounce
- Labels crossfade from regular to semibold while the semibold copy holds the width, so neighbours never shift
- When a label or count changes, the option and the whole control morph to the new width and the pill follows; a new count blurs in
- Pressing gives the pill a little (scale 0.97); dragging it across the options selects as you go
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- If it doesn't fit, it scrolls sideways with soft edges on the sides that hide options and keeps the active one in view
- Touch screens: options are at least 40px tall; a tap picks on lift, so swiping to scroll never picks by accident
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: date-range-picker, filter-menu, data-table

## Setup Guide (Pro)

Onboarding panel with a progress bar and collapsible task groups that strike through when done

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/setup-guide
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/setup-guide.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/setup-guide`

### When to use

- Onboarding with several areas, each made of a few steps that build on each other
- A floating guide in a dashboard corner that people can fold away and come back to

### When not to use

- A single short list of steps – the Progress Tracker is lighter
- Steps that can be done in any order – here each task unlocks the next

### Usage

```tsx
import { SetupGuide } from "@/components/ui/setup-guide";

const groups = [
  {
    id: "workspace",
    title: "Set up your workspace",
    tasks: [
      { id: "name", label: "Choose a workspace name" },
      { id: "invite", label: "Invite your teammates" },
    ],
  },
  { id: "verify", title: "Verify your account", tasks: [{ id: "email", label: "Confirm your email", done: true }] },
];

export function Onboarding() {
  return <SetupGuide groups={groups} onChange={save} onClose={hideGuide} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| groups | `SetupGroup[]` |  | Groups with an id, a title and tasks; each task has an id, a label and an optional done flag |
| title | `string` | `"Setup guide"` | Heading above the bar |
| onEdit | `() => void` |  | Shows an Edit link in the header |
| onClose | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button in the header |
| onChange | `(done: string[]) => void` |  | Called with the ids of all finished tasks |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the panel |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between groups, tasks and header buttons
- Enter / Space: Open or close a group, tick or untick a task

### Accessibility

- Group headers are buttons with aria-expanded, the closed panels are inert
- Tasks that are not unlocked yet are disabled; finished ones are pressed toggle buttons
- The bar is a progressbar with its percentage as value

### Motion

- Groups unfold smoothly; a finished group is struck through, folds away and opens the next one
- Reduced motion turns the transitions off

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: progress-tracker, profile-menu

## Stepper Form (Pro)

A multi-step flow for onboarding and setup – steps that fill and check off, sliding steps, a card that morphs to each step, inline validation and a success state

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/stepper-form
- Section: Components · Inputs
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/stepper-form.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/stepper-form`

### When to use

- Onboarding, checkout or setup wizards where one long form would feel like too much at once
- Flows whose later steps depend on earlier answers, ending in a review before anything is created

### When not to use

- Two or three fields – a single form is faster
- Settings people jump around in freely – use tabs or sections instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { StepperForm, StepperField, StepperInput, StepperTags, StepperChoices, StepperReview, type Step } from "@/components/ui/stepper-form";

type Values = { name: string; slug: string; invites: string[]; plan: string };

const steps: Step<Values>[] = [
  {
    id: "workspace",
    title: "Workspace",
    heading: "Name your workspace",
    render: ({ values, setValues }) => (
      <>
        <StepperField name="name" label="Workspace name">
          <StepperInput value={values.name} onChange={(e) => setValues({ name: e.target.value, slug: slugify(e.target.value) })} />
        </StepperField>
        <StepperField name="slug" label="Workspace URL">
          <StepperInput prefix="acme.app/" value={values.slug} onChange={(e) => setValues({ slug: e.target.value })} />
        </StepperField>
      </>
    ),
    validate: (v) => ({ name: v.name.trim() ? undefined : "Give your workspace a name" }),
  },
  {
    id: "team",
    title: "Team",
    render: ({ values, setValues }) => (
      <StepperField name="invites" label="Email addresses" optional>
        <StepperTags value={values.invites} onChange={(invites) => setValues({ invites })} />
      </StepperField>
    ),
  },
  {
    id: "plan",
    title: "Plan",
    render: ({ values, setValues }) => (
      <StepperChoices label="Plan" value={values.plan} options={plans} onChange={(plan) => setValues({ plan })} />
    ),
  },
  {
    id: "review",
    title: "Review",
    render: ({ values, goTo }) => (
      <StepperReview
        onEdit={goTo}
        rows={[
          { label: "Workspace", value: values.name, step: "workspace" },
          { label: "Plan", value: values.plan, step: "plan" },
        ]}
      />
    ),
  },
];

export function Onboarding() {
  return (
    <StepperForm<Values>
      steps={steps}
      initialValues={{ name: "", slug: "", invites: [], plan: "pro" }}
      submitLabel="Create workspace"
      onComplete={(values) => api.createWorkspace(values)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `Step<V>[]` |  | { id, title, heading?, description?, render(ctx), validate?(values) } – render gets values, setValues, errors, goTo and next; validate returns messages by field name |
| initialValues | `V` |  | Values shared by all steps, so Back and Edit keep what was entered |
| onComplete | `(values: V) => void \| Promise<void>` |  | Runs on the last step; a promise shows the submitting label until it settles, a thrown error is shown next to the button |
| initialStep | `number` | `0` | Index of the first step shown |
| step | `number` |  | Controlled step index; pair with onStepChange |
| onStepChange | `(step: number) => void` |  | Called whenever the step changes |
| submitLabel | `string` | `"Finish"` | Label of the button on the last step |
| submittingLabel | `string` | `"Creating…"` | Label while onComplete runs |
| success | `(values: V, reset: () => void) => ReactNode` |  | Replaces the steps once done – StepperSuccess gives the popping check, a heading and a line |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| StepperField | `{ name, label, hint?, optional?, children }` |  | Label, control and inline message for the field name in validate; the control shakes when Continue finds a problem |
| StepperInput | `InputHTMLAttributes & { prefix? }` |  | A text field wired to its StepperField; prefix shows fixed text like "acme.app/" |
| StepperTags | `{ value, onChange, validate?, max?, placeholder? }` |  | Entries as chips – emails by default; Enter, comma or a pasted list add, × or Backspace remove |
| StepperChoices | `{ value, onChange, options, label }` |  | Selectable cards { value, title, aside?, description?, badge? } as a radio group with a gliding ring |
| StepperReview | `{ rows, onEdit? }` |  | A summary { label, value, step? } – rows with a step get an Edit link (pass goTo) |

### Keyboard

- ↵: Continues (in a chip field: adds the typed entry first, Continue when it's empty)
- Tab: Moves through the fields, then Back and Continue
- ← / →: In the plan cards: moves and selects; ↵ picks and continues
- , / ⌫: In a chip field: comma adds, Backspace in the empty field removes the last chip

### Accessibility

- The steps are an ordered list with aria-current="step"; finished steps are buttons that jump back
- On narrow screens the list stays for screen readers while the compact "Step 2 of 4" text shows on screen
- The new step's first field (or its heading) gets the focus; after a failed Continue the first invalid field does
- Fields carry aria-invalid and point to their message with aria-describedby; "Step 2 of 4: Team" and errors are announced in a polite live region
- Continue looks dimmed while the step isn't valid but still answers, so keyboard and screen reader users hear what's missing

### Motion

- A finished step swaps its number for a check that draws itself in
- Steps slide in from the side you're heading to with a short fade, while the old one slides out the other way
- The card glides to the height of each step; the primary button glides to the width of its new label
- An invalid field shakes once and its message folds in; chips pop in and fold away
- The plan ring glides between cards; the success check pops in
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 520px and works down to 320px
- Below 420px the steps collapse to "Step 2 of 4 · Team", plan cards stack and review rows wrap
- Touch screens get 16px fields (no zoom on iOS) and buttons of at least 40px; the footer sticks to the bottom in long pages
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: setup-guide, progress-tracker, combobox, segmented-control

---

## Thinking Loader (Free)

A small working pill for AI replies – an eight-ray spinner and a shimmering label that rolls through phases and settles on a check

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/thinking-loader
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/thinking-loader.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/thinking-loader`

### When to use

- The wait between sending a prompt and the first streamed token – one line that says what the model is doing
- Agent and pipeline steps with real labels: searching, reading, running a tool, writing
- Inline in a chat bubble or next to a button where a full panel would be too much

### When not to use

- When people should see the sources and every step – use Thinking State
- Page or data loading with no phases – a skeleton or a plain spinner reads calmer
- Waits under half a second – the loader would only flash

### Usage

```tsx
import { ThinkingLoader } from "@/components/ui/thinking-loader";

export function AssistantPending({ streaming }: { streaming: boolean }) {
  return (
    <ThinkingLoader
      phases={["Thinking", "Searching the web", "Reading sources", "Writing response"]}
      interval={2200}
      done={streaming}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| phases | `string[]` | `["Thinking", "Searching the web", "Reading sources", "Writing response"]` | Labels to walk through, one after another |
| interval | `number` | `2200` | Time per phase in ms when the phase isn't controlled |
| phase | `number` |  | Controlled index into phases – the timer stops and the loader shows this phase |
| loop | `boolean` | `false` | Start over after the last phase instead of holding it |
| done | `boolean` | `false` | Turns the spinner into a check and the label into doneLabel; setting it back to false starts over |
| doneLabel | `string \| ((seconds: number) => string)` | `(s) => `Thought for ${s}s`` | Label once done – a function gets the seconds since the loader started |
| size | `"sm" \| "md"` | `"md"` | 28 or 34px tall |
| variant | `"pill" \| "plain"` | `"pill"` | A bordered capsule, or just the spinner and the label |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- role="status" with aria-live="polite": screen readers hear each new phase and the done label once
- The spinner, the check and the label rolling out are aria-hidden; the shimmer copy has empty alt text, so labels are read once

### Motion

- Eight rays fade one after another, so the spinner turns without rotating
- A light sweeps over the label while it works
- On a new phase the old label rolls up and blurs out, the new one rolls in, and the pill glides to its new width
- Done: the spinner shrinks away while the check grows in and draws itself; the label stops shimmering
- With prefers-reduced-motion the labels switch instantly and the spinner and shimmer stand still

### Responsive

- Sizes to its label; long phases stay on one line, so keep them short (two to four words)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Map phases to real events (tool calls, retrieval, first token) with the phase prop when you have them; the timer is a fallback
- Set done when the first token arrives and swap the loader for the streamed message shortly after

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: thinking-state, ai-answer, chat-composer

---

## Thinking State (Pro)

AI working panel with a live timer, searched sources and thinking steps that appear one by one

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/thinking-state
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/thinking-state.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/thinking-state`

### When to use

- Showing what an AI assistant is doing while it works: searching, reading, drafting
- Long-running tasks where a visible trail of steps builds trust and keeps people waiting patiently

### When not to use

- Short waits under a second – a simple spinner or shimmer is enough
- Exact progress you can measure – use a progress bar with a percentage

### Usage

```tsx
import { ThinkingState } from "@/components/ui/thinking-state";

const steps = [
  { kind: "search", label: "Searched", sources: [{ label: "acme.com" }, { label: "+4 more" }] },
  { kind: "step", label: "Reading the sources" },
  { kind: "step", label: "Drafting your answer" },
];

export function AssistantMessage() {
  return <ThinkingState steps={steps} onDone={(seconds) => console.log(seconds)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| steps | `ThinkingStep[]` |  | Searches and thinking steps, revealed in order. Sources can link out (href) and show a tooltip; moreSources hide behind a “+N more” chip |
| doneLabel | `string` | `"Finished thinking"` | Label of the final row |
| stepMs | `number` | `1300` | Pause between two steps, in ms |
| loop | `boolean` | `false` | Starts over a few seconds after finishing |
| onDone | `(seconds: number) => void` |  | Called once all steps are done |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: Collapse or expand the steps (on the header), or show more sources
- Tab: Move through the source links – each shows its tooltip on focus

### Accessibility

- The header is a button with aria-expanded, so the steps can be collapsed
- New steps are announced politely through an aria-live list

### Motion

- The header shimmers with a live timer while thinking, then turns into “Worked for …”
- Steps fade up one after another and the timeline grows down to each new node
- Sources pop in one by one; the active step pulses and shimmers
- Hovering a source shows its link as a tooltip; “+N more” reveals the remaining sources
- At the end a blue check pops in and draws its tick
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything appears without animation

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: chat-composer, progress-tracker

### When not to use

### Usage

```tsx
import { Kbd, TipsPanel } from "@/components/ui/tips-panel";

const tips = [

];

export function Tips() {

}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tips | `Tip[]` |  | id, title, description, action, doneLabel, primary and onAction |
| title | `string` | `"Tips"` | Heading in the gray tray |
| onClose | `() => void` |  | Shows a Close button in the footer |
| closeLabel | `string` | `"Close"` | Text of the Close button |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the tray |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move between the tip actions and Close
- Enter / Space: Take the focused action

### Accessibility

- Each tip is a list item with a real button; the done state is announced as a status
- The counter in the heading is a polite live region

### Motion

- Tips fade in one after another; a taken tip pops into its done state
- Reduced motion turns both off

### Responsive

- Set --ui-tp-max-height on the panel to change how tall the list grows before it scrolls (420px by default)
- Three columns, two below 560px panel width, one below 380px – based on the panel's own width
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: setup-guide, decision-inbox

---

## Toaster (Pro)

Calm toasts from anywhere – a stack that fans out on hover, promise toasts that morph from spinner to check, swipe to dismiss

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/toaster
- Section: Components · Feedback
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/toaster.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/toaster`

### When to use

- Short confirmations after an action – saved, copied, sent, moved to trash (with Undo)
- Background work people started and want to hear back from – uploads, syncs, exports (toast.promise)
- Errors that don't block the page, e.g. a sync that failed and can be retried later

### When not to use

- Errors in a form – show them next to the field
- Anything people must read or decide on – use a dialog or an inline banner
- Long-running progress with details – a progress panel or tracker fits better

### Usage

```tsx
import { Toaster, toast } from "@/components/ui/toaster";

// Once, near the root of the app
export function App() {
  return (
    <>
      <Routes />
      <Toaster position="bottom-right" />
    </>
  );
}

// Anywhere – no hook or context needed
function save() {
  toast.success("Draft saved", { description: "Q3 Board Report · all changes kept" });
}

function remove(file: File) {
  trash(file.id);
  toast("File moved to trash", {
    description: file.name,
    action: { label: "Undo", onClick: () => restore(file.id) },
  });
}

function upload(file: File) {
  toast.promise(api.upload(file), {
    loading: { title: "Uploading report…", description: file.name },
    success: (res) => ({ title: "Report uploaded", description: `Shared with ${res.people} people` }),
    error: (err) => ({ title: "Upload failed", description: String(err) }),
  });
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| position | `"top-left" \| "top-center" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-left" \| "bottom-center" \| "bottom-right"` | `"bottom-right"` | Corner or edge the stack sits in; new toasts come in from that edge |
| inline | `boolean` | `false` | Positions the stack inside the nearest positioned ancestor instead of the viewport |
| id | `string` |  | Only shows toasts sent with { toaster: id } – for a second, separate stack |
| duration | `number` | `4000` | Default time on screen in ms; each toast can override it, Infinity keeps it open |
| visibleToasts | `number` | `3` | Toasts visible at once; older ones wait (with a paused timer) until there's room |
| expand | `boolean` | `false` | Always shows the stack fanned out instead of on hover and focus |
| offset | `number` | `24 (20 inline)` | Distance from the edges in px; phones always use 12px gutters |
| gap | `number` | `10` | Space between toasts when fanned out, in px |
| hotkey | `string \| null` | `"F8"` | Key (KeyboardEvent.key or .code) that moves focus to the newest toast |
| hairline | `boolean` | `true` | A 1px line along the bottom that runs down with the timer and stops when it pauses |
| closeButton | `boolean` | `true` | Small close button on hover and focus – always visible on touch screens |
| label | `string` | `"Notifications"` | Name of the region for screen readers (the hotkey is added) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the region |
| toast(title, options?) | `(ReactNode, ToastOptions) => ToastId` |  | Shows a plain toast; also toast.success, toast.error, toast.info and toast.loading. Returns the id |
| toast.promise(promise, messages, options?) | `<T>(Promise<T> \| () => Promise<T>, { loading, success, error }) => Promise<T>` |  | A loading toast that turns into success or error; each message is a title, { title, description } or a function of the result |
| toast.dismiss(id?) | `(ToastId?) => void` |  | Closes one toast, or all of them without an id |
| ToastOptions | `{ id?, description?, action?: { label, onClick }, duration?, icon?, toaster?, onDismiss? }` |  | Pass an existing id to update that toast in place (the timer restarts, the text crossfades). action.onClick closes the toast unless it calls event.preventDefault() |

### Keyboard

- F8: Moves focus to the newest toast and fans the stack out
- Tab: Goes from toast to toast, through their action and close buttons
- Esc: Closes the focused toast (or the newest) and moves focus to the next one; focus returns where it was after the last

### Accessibility

- The stack is a labelled region ("Notifications (F8)"); every toast is focusable
- New and updated toasts are read out in a polite status region – errors in an alert region, so they come first
- The timer pauses while the pointer or keyboard focus is in the stack and while the tab is hidden, so nothing vanishes mid-read
- Swiping is never the only way out: there's Esc and a named close button
- Icons are decorative; color is limited to the success and error icons, the text says what happened

### Motion

- New toasts lift in from the edge; the ones behind move back, shrink a little and peek out
- Hover or focus fans the stack out into a list – every toast is measured, so positions and heights glide
- Promise toasts: the spinning arc closes into a ring while a check or cross draws in; the text crossfades and the card resizes
- Closed toasts fade and sink a few pixels while the rest of the stack moves up; swiped toasts fly out in the swipe direction, short swipes rubber-band back
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly – only the spinner keeps turning

### Responsive

- 356px wide on larger screens; under 600px it spans the width with 12px gutters (and respects the home indicator)
- Touch: tap the stack to fan it out, swipe sideways or down to dismiss; close and action buttons get bigger hit areas
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Render <Toaster /> once; call toast() from event handlers or effects, not during render
- Use toast.promise for async work instead of separate loading and success toasts
- Keep titles to a few words and put details in description

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: notification-stack, progress-tracker, dropzone

---

## Tool Call Card (Free)

An agent's tool call in one line – live timer, status and summary, folds open to highlighted arguments and result with copy, retry on errors and a group that sums them up

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/tool-call-card
- Section: Components · Agents
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/tool-call-card.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/tool-call-card`

### When to use

- Tool and function calls in an agent chat or run log – what was called, with what, and what came back
- Agents that call several tools per turn – wrap them in ToolCallGroup so the answer isn't buried under cards
- Developer-facing views where people need to copy the exact arguments or result to debug

### When not to use

- Plain reasoning with no tool calls – use Thinking State or Thinking Loader
- End users who never care about JSON – show a one-line status instead and keep the details in a log
- Huge payloads (megabytes of JSON) – trim or paginate them first; the card renders the whole string

### Usage

```tsx
import { ToolCallCard, ToolCallGroup } from "@/components/ui/tool-call-card";

export function ToolCalls({ calls }: { calls: ToolCall[] }) {
  return (
    <ToolCallGroup>
      {calls.map((call) => (
        <ToolCallCard
          key={call.id}
          name={call.name}
          summary={call.summary}
          status={call.status}
          args={call.args}
          result={call.result}
          error={call.error}
          startedAt={call.startedAt}
          duration={call.durationMs}
          onRetry={() => retryToolCall(call.id)}
        />
      ))}
    </ToolCallGroup>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` |  | Tool name as the agent calls it, shown in mono – e.g. "search_web" |
| status | `"running" \| "success" \| "error"` |  | Spinner with a live timer, check with the duration, or a red "Failed" |
| summary | `ReactNode` |  | Short human summary next to the name; truncates with an ellipsis |
| icon | `ReactNode` | `wrench icon` | Icon in the tile on the left – a 16px stroke SVG fits best |
| args | `unknown` |  | Arguments – objects are pretty-printed and highlighted, JSON strings are parsed; the section is hidden when undefined |
| result | `unknown` |  | What the tool returned – like args; other strings are shown as plain text. While running without a result, "Waiting for result…" is shown |
| error | `string` |  | Error message, shown in the body when status is "error" |
| startedAt | `number` |  | Start time in ms since epoch – the live timer counts from here instead of from when the card turned running |
| duration | `number` |  | Final duration in ms – otherwise the time measured while the card was running |
| defaultOpen | `boolean` | `false` | Start expanded (uncontrolled) |
| open | `boolean` |  | Expanded state (controlled) |
| onOpenChange | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called when the header is toggled |
| openOnError | `boolean` | `true` | Opens the card when the call fails and closes it on the next run, unless someone toggled it by hand (uncontrolled only) |
| onRetry | `() => void` |  | Shows a Retry button next to the error message |
| maxCodeHeight | `number` | `220` | Height in px after which arguments and result are capped with a fade and a "Show all" toggle |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| ToolCallGroup · children | `ToolCallCard elements` |  | The cards – the group reads their icon, status and duration props for its header, so pass them as direct children |
| ToolCallGroup · label | `string` | `"Used N tools"` | Header label once nothing is running |
| ToolCallGroup · runningLabel | `string` | `"Using tools…"` | Shimmering header label while any card is running |
| ToolCallGroup · duration | `number` |  | Total in ms – otherwise the sum of the cards' duration props, or the time measured while any card was running |
| ToolCallGroup · defaultOpen / open / onOpenChange | `boolean / boolean / (open) => void` | `false` | Expanded state, uncontrolled or controlled |
| ToolCallGroup · className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the headers, copy buttons, Show all and Retry; content of closed cards is skipped
- Enter / Space: On a header: expands or collapses the card or the group

### Accessibility

- Headers are real buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the body
- Closed bodies are inert, so they can't be focused or read until opened
- A polite live region per card announces "search_web running", "finished" or "failed: …"; the group announces "Using tools…" and "Used 3 tools"
- Copy buttons are labelled "Copy arguments" / "Copy result" and switch to "Copied"; icons are aria-hidden
- Errors use text and an icon, not only red

### Motion

- The body grows with grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr and fades in; the chevron turns
- Status changes blur in; the success check draws itself; the spinner turns while running
- Copy morphs into a check for 1.4s; Show all opens the capped block to its full height
- In the group, new tool icons pop into the stack and "Using tools…" shimmers while anything runs
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly and the shimmer is off

### Responsive

- Fills its container; name and summary truncate with an ellipsis, the status never wraps – works down to ~320px
- Code wraps long lines instead of scrolling sideways
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Map your agent's tool-call events 1:1: status running on the call, success or error on the result; pass startedAt from the event for an exact timer
- Write summary in past tense when done ("Searched…") and present progressive while running ("Searching…")
- Pass args and result as objects – stringify nothing yourself; redact secrets before they reach the card
- Wrap all calls of one assistant turn in a single ToolCallGroup and keep cards as direct children

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: thinking-loader, thinking-state, ai-answer

---

## Usage Meter (Pro)

Plan usage and AI credits – a stacked credits meter by category, daily sparkline, limits and a button that speaks up near the limit

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/usage-meter
- Section: Components · Data display
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/usage-meter.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/usage-meter`

### When to use

- The usage or billing page of a SaaS or AI product – credits, tokens, minutes or messages per billing cycle
- Showing what the usage went into (chat, search, images, API) next to plan limits like seats and storage
- Nudging people to top up or upgrade right where they see they're running out

### When not to use

- Long-term trends over many months – a line chart like the KPI Chart reads better
- More than about five categories – the bar gets too thin; group the small ones into "Other"

### Usage

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { UsageMeter } from "@/components/ui/usage-meter";

export function Usage({ usage }) {
  const [period, setPeriod] = useState("month");
  const data = usage[period]; // { used, limits, daily } per period from your API

  return (
    <UsageMeter
      title="Acme AI"
      plan="Pro plan"
      total={10000}
      used={data.used} // [{ label: "Chat", value: 3980 }, { label: "Search", value: 1640 }, …]
      limits={[
        { label: "Seats", used: 8, total: 10 },
        { label: "Storage", used: 3.2, total: 5, unit: "GB" },
        { label: "Projects", used: 12, total: null }, // unlimited
      ]}
      daily={data.daily} // [{ label: "Oct 1", value: 312 }, …, { label: "Oct 17", value: null }]
      periods={[
        { id: "month", label: "This month" },
        { id: "last", label: "Last month" },
        { id: "7d", label: "7 days" },
      ]}
      period={period}
      onPeriodChange={setPeriod}
      resetAt="2026-10-17"
      onUpgrade={(state) => (state === "ok" ? openPlans() : openTopUp())}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| total | `number` |  | Credits included in the plan – the bar's full width |
| used | `{ label: string; value: number; color?: string }[]` |  | What the credits went into in the shown period. Without colors the parts get shades of the accent, then grays; each label keeps its shade |
| limits | `{ label; used; total?: number \| null; unit?; decimals? }[]` |  | Thin meters below, e.g. seats and storage. Leave total out (or null) for unlimited – shown as "of ∞" on a striped track |
| periods | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | Options of the period switch; no switch when left out |
| period | `string` |  | Controlled period id – pass the matching used, limits and daily with it |
| defaultPeriod | `string` |  | Starting period when uncontrolled; defaults to the first option |
| onPeriodChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called when a period is picked |
| resetAt | `Date \| string \| number` |  | When the credits reset – shown as "Resets in 9 days", the date on hover |
| daily | `{ label: string; value: number \| null }[]` |  | Usage per day for the sparkline; null for days still to come, shown as flat stubs |
| onUpgrade | `(state: "ok" \| "warn" \| "limit") => void` |  | Called by the button with the current state |
| title | `string` | `"Usage"` | Card title, e.g. the workspace or product name |
| plan | `string` |  | Plan name in front of the reset date |
| unit | `string` | `"credits"` | Unit of the main meter |
| warnAt | `number` | `0.8` | Share (0–1) from which the meter and the limits warn |
| upgradeLabel | `string` | `"Upgrade"` | Button text while there is room left (a quiet button) |
| topUpLabel | `string` | `"Add credits"` | Button text near and at the limit (a solid button) |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Reaches the period switch, the bar, the sparkline and the button
- ← / →: Switch: picks the previous or next period. Bar: steps through the categories. Sparkline: steps through the days
- Esc: Hides the category or day readout

### Accessibility

- A section labelled by its title; the bar and every limit are meters with their value as text ("7,420 of 10,000 credits")
- The period switch is a radio group with a roving tab stop
- The category tooltip is a polite live region, so stepping through the bar reads each part
- Running low and reaching the limit are announced in a polite live region; amber is never the only signal – the text says it too

### Motion

- On first view the bar fills from zero and every number counts up, in one frame loop so numbers and widths stay in step
- Switching periods: the white pill glides to the new option, numbers roll to their new values and the parts glide to their new widths
- A category that drops out shrinks to nothing on the bar while its legend row folds away; the card glides to its new height
- Hovering a part dims the others and highlights its legend row; the tooltip glides along the bar
- Near the limit a small amber dot pops in and the button turns solid with a gentle nudge, its width gliding to the new label
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 460px; at 400px and below the switch gets its own row and the limits stack as rows
- Works down to 320px wide; long labels end with an ellipsis, numbers and units never split
- Touch: tapping a part or a legend row shows its value, targets grow to 36–38px
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: kpi-chart, breakdown-chart, billing-schedule, progress-tracker

## Writing Assistant (Pro)

AI chat card with a soft gradient glow, suggestions, streaming replies and live voice dictation

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/components/writing-assistant
- Section: Components · Chat
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/writing-assistant.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/writing-assistant`

### When to use

- A small AI helper inside an editor, CRM or sidebar – rewrite, shorten, translate or draft
- Landing pages that should show an assistant you can actually try, including voice input

### When not to use

- Long conversations with files, tools and model settings – use the Chat Composer or the AI Workspace block
- When you can't send voice to the browser's speech service – set speech="simulate" or hide the mic

### Usage

```tsx
import { WritingAssistant } from "@/components/ui/writing-assistant";

export function Helper() {
  return (
    <WritingAssistant
      name="Quill"
      tagline="Your writing companion."
      respond={async (message) => {
        const res = await fetch("/api/write", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ message }) });
        return (await res.json()).text;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | `string` | `"Quill"` | Assistant name on top |
| tagline | `string` | `"Your writing companion."` | Line under the name |
| greeting | `string` | `"What should we write?"` | Big line on the welcome screen |
| suggestions | `string[]` |  | Chips that send themselves as a message |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Ask anything…"` | Placeholder of the prompt field |
| respond | `(message) => string \| Promise<string>` |  | Your answer for a message; a sample writer is used by default |
| speech | `"auto" \| "simulate"` | `"auto"` | auto uses the browser's speech recognition when available, simulate always plays a sample take |
| dictation | `string` |  | Sentence used for simulated dictation |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Sends what's in the prompt field
- Shift / Enter: Starts a new line – the field grows up to four lines, then scrolls
- Tab: Moves through the suggestions, the field, Send, the mic and New chat

### Accessibility

- The mic is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a label that says what it does next
- New messages are announced politely; the typing dots carry a label
- Everything works with the keyboard; dictation is optional

### Motion

- The glow keeps drifting in the lower half; the welcome view hands over to the chat with a short rise
- While listening, the mic turns dark with three calm bars and a soft ring breathing outwards; words appear live in the field
- When you stop speaking, the finished sentence moves into the chat as your message; replies stream in word by word
- With prefers-reduced-motion the glow stands still and replies appear at once

### Responsive

- Fills its container up to 380px wide
- Dictation uses the Web Speech API (Chrome, Edge, Safari) with the page language; elsewhere a short simulated take plays
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Agent Run (Pro)

One autonomous agent run: the plan ticking through its steps, the tool calls, an approval it waits on and the draft it wrote

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/agent-run
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-run.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-run`

### When to use

- The detail view of one autonomous agent run – a background task, a scheduled job, a long workflow
- Runs that pause for a human before they send, pay or publish something

### When not to use

- Back-and-forth conversations with the agent – use Agent Chat
- A list of many runs – use a table with a status column

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentRunScreen } from "@/components/ui/agent-run";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <AgentRunScreen
      title="Prepare the Q3 board update"
      steps={run.steps}
      draft={{ original: memo.before, suggested: memo.after, label: "Board memo – Q3" }}
      onApprove={(stepId) => api.approve(run.id, stepId)}
      onDeny={(stepId) => api.deny(run.id, stepId)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` | `"Prepare the Q3 board update"` | Goal of the run, in the header and above the plan |
| steps | `RunStep[]` | `defaultRunSteps` | Steps with id, title, detail, tool, their tool calls ({ name, summary, icon?, args?, result?, duration }) and an optional approval ({ title, description, risk, details }) the run waits on |
| draft | `{ original: string; suggested: string; label?: string }` | `defaultRunDraft` | Text the agent wrote, shown as an inline diff in the side panel |
| agent | `string` | `"Board prep"` | Name of the agent in the run details |
| autoRun | `boolean` | `true` | Plays the built-in simulation on mount – turn off and drive the steps from your own events |
| onApprove | `(stepId: string) => void` |  | An approval was given; the run carries on |
| onDeny | `(stepId: string) => void` |  | An approval was denied; the run stops at that step |
| onStop | `() => void` |  | Stop run pressed |
| onDone | `() => void` |  | Every step is done |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name in the sidebar |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, the run actions and the panel toggle are real buttons with labels
- The plan marks the current step with aria-current and announces progress; tool calls and approvals announce their status
- Approve and deny work from the keyboard (⌘↵ / Esc), the diff with Tab, Y and N
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app; the run and the side panel scroll on their own
- Below 1000px of main area the side panel becomes a layer that slides in from the right
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, Agent Plan, Tool Call Card, Approval Card, Inline Diff, Thinking Loader and Button (installed with it)

## Analytics (Pro)

Revenue dashboard: key figures, revenue by channel, breakdown, top products and weekly trends

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/analytics
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/analytics.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/analytics`

### When to use

- Revenue, product or marketing dashboards
- Overview pages that combine key figures and charts

### When not to use

- Live monitoring with many changing values – use a denser layout

### Usage

```tsx
import { AnalyticsScreen } from "@/components/ui/analytics";

export default function Page() {
  return <AnalyticsScreen workspace="Acme" user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }} onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name in the sidebar |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, tabs and toolbar actions are real buttons with labels
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, KPI Chart and Button (installed with it)

## App Shell (Pro)

Collapsible sidebar with workspace, menu, projects and account – the frame every screen sits in

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/app-shell
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/app-shell.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/app-shell`

### When to use

- The base of an AI assistant, internal tool or SaaS dashboard
- Building your own screens on the same frame as the other affectUI screens

### When not to use

- Marketing pages – use a block or a plain layout
- Apps with deep, multi-level navigation trees

### Usage

```tsx
import { AppShell } from "@/components/ui/app-shell";

export function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <AppShell active="New chat" workspace="Acme" user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }} onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}>
      <div className="ui-as-page">{children}</div>
    </AppShell>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The page shown next to the sidebar |
| active | `string` |  | Label of the menu item or project that is open |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a menu item or project when it is clicked |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name; its first letter becomes the logo |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom; without an avatar it shows initials |
| nav | `ShellNavItem[]` | `New chat, Folders, Integrations` | Menu items, each { label, icon } |
| projects | `string[]` |  | Project list under the menu |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, projects and the collapse toggle are real buttons with labels
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons

## Evals (Pro)

- Eval dashboards for prompts, agents or LLM features
- Comparing prompt or model versions against a fixed test suite

### When not to use

- Live production monitoring of single requests – use a log or trace view

### Usage

```tsx
import { EvalsScreen } from "@/components/ui/evals";

export default function Page() {
  return <EvalsScreen workspace="Acme" user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }} onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name in the sidebar |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Sidebar items, the version menu, filters and Run eval are real buttons with labels
- Test case rows are focusable and select with Enter or Space
- Prompt changes are reviewed with the keyboard: Tab between changes, Y accepts, N rejects
- Icons are decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- Below 1000px the right column moves under the table; the table scrolls sideways on phones
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

## Onboarding (Pro)

First-run flow of an AI workspace: workspace setup, tool connections, team invites and a first agent, with a getting-started checklist

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/screens/onboarding
- Section: Screens · App screens
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/onboarding.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/onboarding`

### When to use

- The first minutes after sign-up in a workspace or AI product
- Guided setup that people can skip and pick up again later

### When not to use

- Long forms with many required fields – use the Stepper Form
- A single setting – show it inline instead of a whole flow

### Usage

```tsx
import { OnboardingScreen } from "@/components/ui/onboarding";

export default function Page() {
  return (
    <OnboardingScreen
      workspace="Acme"
      user={{ name: "Alex Morgan" }}
      defaultStep={1}
      onComplete={(values) => api.finishOnboarding(values)}
      onNavigate={(label) => router.push(routes[label])}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| defaultStep | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `2` | Step shown first; the steps before it count as done |
| onComplete | `(values: OnboardingValues) => void` |  | Called after Create agent (or skipping the last step) with workspace, slug, team size, tools, invites, role and template |
| onNavigate | `(label: string) => void` |  | Called with the label of a sidebar item or a next step (Chat, Integrations, Analytics) |
| workspace | `string` | `"Acme"` | Workspace name in the sidebar, the greeting and the first field |
| user | `{ name: string; avatar?: string }` | `{ name: "Alex Morgan" }` | Account at the bottom of the sidebar; the first name is used in the greeting |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Each step is a form: Enter continues, the primary button submits
- Progress is a progressbar with the step name as its value text; the checklist marks the current step with aria-current
- Tool toggles are switches, templates a radio group; email chips can be removed with their button or Backspace
- Step transitions and checkmarks turn off with prefers-reduced-motion

### Responsive

- Fills its container – give it the full viewport height in your app
- The checklist sits beside the step card on wide panels and moves below it on narrow ones
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"; colors are CSS variables on .ui-as

### Requirements

- React 19
- @hugeicons/react
- @hugeicons/core-free-icons
- App Shell, Segmented Control and Button (installed with it)

---
