## Agent Gallery (Pro)

Slim gradient panels with one open product screen in the middle – pick a panel and it glides open

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/agent-gallery
- Section: Blocks · Feature sections
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-gallery.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-gallery`

### When to use

- Showing several agents, workflows or product areas on a landing page, one at a time with a real-looking screen
- Feature sections that should feel explorable rather than a static grid

### When not to use

- Two or three items – a simple tab switch reads faster
- Content people need to compare side by side

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentGallery } from "@/components/ui/agent-gallery";

export function AgentsSection() {
  return <AgentGallery title="Agents that run your playbook" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` |  | Heading above the panels |
| subtitle | `string` |  | Line under the heading |
| items | `GalleryItem[]` |  | Each { id, name, description, colors: [strong, soft], trigger, steps, skills, guardrail } – drives the panel colors, the label and the screen |
| defaultIndex | `number` | `the middle item` | Panel that starts open |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: With focus in the panels, opens the previous or next one
- Tab: Moves through the side panels and the arrow buttons

### Accessibility

- Marked as a carousel; side panels are buttons labelled “Show …”
- The caption under the open panel is announced when it changes

### Motion

- The picked panel widens into the middle while the open one folds into a slim panel – one smooth width transition
- Side panels show the artwork muted and come to full color on hover; the screen slides in after the panel has opened
- With prefers-reduced-motion panels switch instantly

### Responsive

- Follows its own width: below 760px the open panel fills the width with one slim panel peeking on each side
- Every panel shares one gradient artwork drawn in CSS – only two colors per item change, so it scales crisply
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

---

## AI Workspace (Pro)

Complete assistant app – sidebar, welcome, streaming chat and projects, built on the Chat Composer

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/ai-workspace
- Section: Blocks · Productivity
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/ai-workspace.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/ai-workspace`

### When to use

- The main screen of an AI assistant or copilot inside your product
- Internal tools where people chat with your data and group work into projects

### When not to use

- A small chat widget in a corner – use the Chat Composer on its own

### Usage

```tsx
import { AiWorkspace } from "@/components/ui/ai-workspace";

export function Assistant() {
  return (
    <AiWorkspace
      userName="Lena"
      respond={async (message, history) => {
        const res = await fetch("/api/chat", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify({ message, history }) });
        return (await res.json()).answer;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| respond | `(message, history) => Promise<string>` |  | Your model call – the answer streams in word by word. Demo answers without it |
| userName | `string` | `"Lena"` | Shown in the greeting and the sidebar |
| userAvatar | `string` |  | Image for the sidebar footer |
| workspace | `ReactNode` | `"N"` | Initial or logo in the top-left tile |
| pinned | `string[]` |  | Pinned assistants in the sidebar – pinned projects are added automatically |
| conversations | `Conversation[]` |  | Recent chats with their messages |
| projects | `Project[]` |  | Projects with name, description, days since update and pinned |

### Keyboard

- Enter: Send a message in the composer
- Escape: Close menus and the create-project dialog
- Tab: Move through sidebar, header, chat and projects

### Accessibility

- Menus are real menus with radio items, the dialog is modal and labelled, the collapsed sidebar is inert
- New answers are announced politely while they stream in

### Motion

- The sidebar collapses smoothly, answers stream in, views fade in, menus drop in
- Reduced motion turns these off

### Responsive

- Below 720px of width the sidebar becomes an overlay and the project grid turns into one column
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
- Chat Composer – installed automatically with the CLI

Related: chat-composer, thinking-state, comments-panel

---

## App Directory (Pro)

Browse, search and connect integrations – categories, filters and app cards with a connect flow

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/app-directory
- Section: Blocks · Integrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/app-directory.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/app-directory`

### When to use

- An integrations or marketplace page in a SaaS product
- Settings screens where people connect and disconnect third-party tools

### When not to use

- Two or three integrations – a short list in settings is enough
- Hundreds of apps – add server-side search and paging

### Usage

```tsx
import { AppDirectory } from "@/components/ui/app-directory";

export function Integrations() {
  return <AppDirectory apps={apps} onToggle={(app, connected) => save(app.id, connected)} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| apps | `App[]` |  | id, name, vendor, description, categories, logo, tile color, essential and connected |
| categories | `AppCategory[]` |  | Sidebar entries with id, label and icon – essentials and all are built in |
| title | `string` | `"Integrations"` | Heading inside the card |
| subtitle | `string` |  | Line under the heading |
| onToggle | `(app: App, connected: boolean) => void` |  | Called after an app was connected or disconnected |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the block |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move through search, filter, categories and the connect buttons
- Escape: Close the filter menu

### Accessibility

- Search has a label, the filter is a menu of radio items, the current category is marked
- Connect buttons say which app they connect; the result heading is a live region

### Motion

- Cards fade in, connecting shows a spinner, the filter menu drops in – reduced motion turns this off

### Responsive

- Three columns with a sidebar on wide containers; below 820px the categories become a row of chips and the grid two columns; below 560px one column
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Client Context (Pro)

A client workspace with live numbers and a shared context timeline – switch clients, search, filter and add notes or files

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/client-context
- Section: Blocks · Productivity
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/client-context.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/client-context`

### When to use

- Agency, accounting and CRM tools where a team keeps goals, files and decisions per client
- Product pages for AI tools – show the context that makes every answer fit the client

### When not to use

- A full activity log with hundreds of events – page or virtualise it instead
- Real-time collaboration – the timeline adds entries locally and leaves syncing to you

### Usage

```tsx
import { ClientContext } from "@/components/ui/client-context";

export function ClientPage() {
  return (
    <ClientContext
      me={{ name: "Lena Hart", avatar: "/avatars/lena.jpg" }}
      onAddContext={(clientId, text, files) => api.addContext(clientId, { text, files })}
      onCreateClient={(name) => api.createClient(name)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| clients | `ContextClient[]` |  | Each { id, name, meta, mark, kpis, reports, context } – the switcher lists them all |
| context entries | `ContextEntry[]` |  | note ("@Report name" becomes a mention), report, files (type pdf · xlsx · csv · doc) or integration { app, connected } |
| me | `{ name, avatar? }` |  | Author of new context |
| onAddContext | `(clientId, text, files) => void` |  | Called when context is added |
| onCreateClient | `(name) => void` |  | Called when a client is created from the switcher |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ⌘ / Enter: Adds the context you typed
- @: Suggests the client's reports – Enter or Tab inserts the first
- Esc: Closes the switcher, the filter and the mention suggestions
- Tab: Moves through the switcher, tabs, search, filter and composer

### Accessibility

- Tabs are a tablist with a labelled panel; the client switcher, filter and mention suggestions are listboxes
- KPI cards and financial rows are toggle buttons; reports are disclosure buttons with aria-expanded
- Search, composer and attachment buttons are labelled; settings are switches

### Motion

- KPI cards rise in one after another and their sparklines draw in; new context slides in at the top
- The tab thumb glides with a little spring, reports fold open, menus pop from their button, sync icons spin while working
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Follows its own width: below 680px the KPIs wrap into two rows, the tabs stretch and search moves below them
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Invoice & Credit Note (Pro)

An invoice and its credit note stacked like paper – switch between them, pick lines to credit, adjust amounts and issue

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/invoice-credit
- Section: Blocks · Billing
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/invoice-credit.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/invoice-credit`

### When to use

- Billing portals and admin tools that show an invoice and let a team credit it
- Product pages for invoicing software – a document that looks real and can be tried

### When not to use

- Printing or PDF generation – render a dedicated print layout instead
- Invoices with dozens of lines – the credit tray is built for a handful

### Usage

```tsx
import { InvoiceCredit } from "@/components/ui/invoice-credit";

export function Billing() {
  return (
    <InvoiceCredit
      invoiceNo="INV-2041"
      creditNo="CN-0117"
      lines={[
        { id: "plan", name: "Growth plan", qty: 1, rate: 1250, tax: 0.2 },
        { id: "api", name: "API calls (per 1k)", qty: 18420, rate: 0.42, tax: 0.2, group: "Metered usage" },
      ]}
      onIssue={(credits, total) => api.issueCreditNote(credits, total)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| seller / buyer | `{ name, lines: string[] }` |  | From and To blocks on the invoice |
| invoiceNo / creditNo | `string` |  | Document numbers shown under Terms |
| invoiceDate / dueDate / period | `string` |  | Dates shown on both documents |
| lines | `InvoiceLine[]` |  | Each { id, name, qty, rate, tax, group? } – lines with a group are listed under a heading |
| currency | `string` | `"$"` | Currency symbol |
| onIssue | `(credits, total) => void` |  | Called when the credit note is issued, with the credited amount per line and the total incl. tax |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the switch, the actions, every line and amount
- Enter: Confirms an amount

### Accessibility

- The switch is a tablist; the sheet in the back is hidden from screen readers and can't be focused
- Credit lines are checkboxes with labels; amounts are labelled per line and stay within the line total

### Motion

- Switching slides the sheets: the chosen one comes forward, the other tucks behind it with only its top edge showing
- Checkmarks draw in; the segmented thumb glides between Invoice and Credit note
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches instantly

### Responsive

- Follows its own width: below 560px the parties stack, the rate and tax columns hide and the credit tray drops the total column
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## KPI Board (Pro)

The top of a dashboard – three trend cards, an overview chart that compares this period with the last, and a focus card; hover shows any day's value and every number rolls when the range changes

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/kpi-board
- Section: Blocks · Analytics
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/kpi-board.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/kpi-board`

### When to use

- The top of a dashboard: a few headline numbers with their trend, one chart that compares this period with the last, and one product or plan in focus
- Sales, growth and usage overviews of a SaaS or AI product, above a table or a list
- When the charts belong together – same range, same filter – and should react as one

### When not to use

- One metric in depth – use KPI Chart or Breakdown Chart
- Parts of a whole (shares, funnels, rankings) – the board only draws trends over time
- Reports that are printed or exported – this is built for pointing and switching

### Usage

```tsx
import { KpiBoard, type KpiBoardData } from "@/components/ui/kpi-board";

const ranges = [
  { id: "7d", label: "Last 7 days" },
  { id: "30d", label: "Last 30 days" },
];

export function Overview({ data }: { data: Record<string, KpiBoardData> }) {
  // data["30d"] = { stats, overview, focus }
  return <KpiBoard data={data} ranges={ranges} defaultRange="30d" compareLabel="vs. last month" />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| data | `Record<string, KpiBoardData>` |  | One data set per range id: { stats, overview, focus } |
| ranges | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | Options of the date range picker |
| range | `string` |  | Controlled range id |
| defaultRange | `string` | `first range` | Starting range when uncontrolled |
| onRangeChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new range |
| segments | `{ id: string; label: string }[]` |  | A filter inside the overview card, e.g. All items / Pro / Team – it only switches that card's lines; no filter when left out |
| segment | `string` |  | Controlled segment id |
| defaultSegment | `string` | `first segment` | Starting segment when uncontrolled |
| onSegmentChange | `(id: string) => void` |  | Called with the new segment |
| compareLabel | `string` | `"vs. last period"` | Words after every change |
| currentLabel | `string` | `"This period"` | Name of the main line in the tooltip and the focus card |
| previousLabel | `string` | `"Last period"` | Name of the comparison line |
| formatMoney | `(value: number) => string` | `$1,234.00` | Formats money values |
| icon | `ReactNode` |  | Icon in the focus card |
| title | `string` |  | Heading on the left of the bar above the cards |
| setup | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | The small button at the top right of the focus card, e.g. Set up |
| action | `{ label: string; onClick: () => void }` |  | The button at the bottom of the focus card |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Through the pickers and the action
- Enter / Space / ↓: On a picker: opens its menu
- ↑ / ↓ / Home / End: In an open menu: moves through the choices
- Enter: Picks the highlighted choice
- Esc: Closes the menu without changing anything

### Accessibility

- Every card is a labelled region with its numbers as text; the charts themselves are decorative
- The pickers are comboboxes with a listbox: the open state, the highlighted and the chosen option are announced
- Changes carry an arrow or a sign next to the color, and the color follows whether the change is good news (lowerIsBetter)

### Motion

- On first view the cards rise in one after another and every line draws itself in from the left
- Switching the range rolls every number in one shared tween while every line is drawn in again from the left
- The filter inside the overview does the same for that card only – the other cards stay still
- Hovering a small card marks the day under the pointer with a dot, its value in a tag and the date on the axis
- Hovering the overview shows a dark tooltip that compares this period with the last at that day
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything switches without movement

### Responsive

- The date range sits above the cards on the right. Three small cards over a wide overview and the focus card; below 820px of container width the two lower cards take a full row each, below 600px everything stacks
- It follows its container, not the window
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Series may have different numbers of points per range (7 days, 30 days, 13 weeks) – each range is drawn in fresh
- A stat's value is the sum of its series; `previous` is the total of the period before and drives the change on the right
- The date range sits in the bar above the cards because it changes all of them; the picker inside the overview is the segment and only switches the overview's own lines (overview.segments)

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: metrics-dashboard, kpi-chart, usage-meter

---

## Logo Marquee (Free)

The endless “Trusted by” strip – a seamless loop that eases to a stop on hover, scrubs with inertia and lifts the hovered logo to colour

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/logo-marquee
- Section: Blocks · Social proof
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/logo-marquee.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/logo-marquee`

### When to use

- A “Trusted by” or “Used by teams at” strip under a hero or above pricing
- Showing more customer, partner or integration logos than fit in one static row

### When not to use

- Three to five logos – a static, centred row reads calmer and needs no motion
- Logos people need to compare or click through – use a grid; a moving target is hard to hit

### Usage

```tsx
import { LogoMarquee } from "@/components/ui/logo-marquee";
import { VercelMark, LinearMark, StripeMark, FigmaMark, NotionMark, GitHubMark } from "./marks";

const logos = [
  { name: "Vercel", svg: <VercelMark />, scale: 0.86 },
  { name: "Linear", svg: <LinearMark />, color: "#5E6AD2" },
  { name: "Stripe", svg: <StripeMark />, color: "#635BFF", href: "/customers/stripe" },
  { name: "Figma", svg: <FigmaMark />, color: "#F24E1E" },
  { name: "Notion", svg: <NotionMark /> },
  { name: "GitHub", svg: <GitHubMark /> },
];

export function TrustedBy() {
  return (
    <section className="py-16">
      <p className="mb-6 text-center text-sm text-neutral-500">Trusted by teams at</p>
      <LogoMarquee logos={logos} rows={2} speed={36} labels="beside" />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| logos | `{ name, svg?, src?, color?, scale?, href? }[]` |  | The logos. svg is a ReactNode – use fill="currentColor" so it follows the muted colour; src takes an image instead. color is the brand colour it lifts to on hover, scale corrects optical size, href makes it a link |
| speed | `number` | `40` | Pixels per second – the same pace on any width |
| direction | `"left" \| "right"` | `"left"` | Which way the first row runs |
| rows | `1 \| 2` | `1` | Two rows split the logos alternately and run in opposite directions |
| gap | `number` | `56` | Space between logos in px; about 60 % of it on narrow containers |
| pauseOnHover | `boolean` | `true` | Ease to a stop while hovered or focused with the keyboard, and speed back up on leave |
| grayscale | `boolean` | `true` | Muted, colourless logos; the hovered one lifts to its brand colour. Off shows full colour and dims the others on hover |
| labels | `"none" \| "below" \| "beside"` | `"none"` | Show the brand name as a small caption under the mark, or beside it like a wordmark |
| label | `string` | `"Logos of companies using the product"` | Accessible name of the strip |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through linked logos; the strip stops and the focused logo is nudged into view

### Accessibility

- A labelled region; each name is read once – the repeated copies that make the loop are aria-hidden and inert
- Keyboard focus stops the strip so a logo never runs away from the focus ring
- Hover and focus stop it too, which covers the WCAG pause requirement for moving content
- Reduced motion shows every logo in a static, wrapping row

### Motion

- The loop repeats a measured set and wraps by exactly its width – no gap, no jump
- One requestAnimationFrame loop eases a velocity per row: hover slows it to a stop, leaving winds it back up
- Drag or swipe to scrub; letting go flings it with inertia before it settles back into its own pace
- Only runs while on screen; edges fade out with a mask

### Responsive

- Container queries make logos and gaps smaller in narrow containers, down to 320px without page overflow
- Touch: horizontal swipes scrub the strip, vertical swipes still scroll the page
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: logo-cluster, text-reveal, gradient-text

---

## Metrics Dashboard (Pro)

Sales overview – KPI cards pick the metric, one chart switches between dotted line and bars, with top products and channels

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/metrics-dashboard.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/metrics-dashboard`

### When to use

- A compact sales or business overview with a handful of headline metrics
- Dashboards where one chart, picked by KPI cards and shown as a line or as bars, says more than a grid of small charts

### When not to use

- Large data sets or drill-downs – the chart shows up to 30 points per period
- A single number – use a KPI card instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { MetricsDashboard } from "@/components/ui/metrics-dashboard";

export function Overview() {
  return (
    <MetricsDashboard
      title="Sales"
      site="Northwind Store"
      defaultRange="30d"
      onExport={(range, metric) => console.log("export", range, metric)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | `string` | `"Sales"` | Title in the bar on top |
| site | `string` | `"Northwind Store"` | Site or workspace shown under the title |
| defaultRange | `"7d" \| "30d" \| "90d"` | `"30d"` | Period to start on – shown as Week, Month and Quarter |
| defaultMetric | `"revenue" \| "orders" \| "aov" \| "refunds"` | `"revenue"` | Metric to start on |
| onExport | `(range, metric) => void` |  | Called when Export is pressed; the button confirms locally either way |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the period switch, Export, the KPI cards, the chart type, Compare and the chart
- ← / →: With the chart focused, moves the inspected point
- Home / End: Jumps to the first or last point

### Accessibility

- Period and chart-type buttons use aria-pressed; the KPI cards are tabs with aria-selected
- The chart has a text label with the range and values; the inspected point is announced through a status tooltip
- Deltas say up or down in text, not only with color – and a falling refund rate counts as good

### Motion

- KPI values and list counts count to their new amounts with tabular numerals
- The chosen KPI card turns fully opaque while the others dim; the line draws in with its dots popping on, bars grow up one after another
- With prefers-reduced-motion values and views switch instantly

### Responsive

- Follows the block's own width with container queries: below 640px the KPI cards form a 2 × 2 grid and the lists stack
- Below 460px the period switch fills the width, figures shrink and the chart is 168px tall
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Task Board (Pro)

Kanban board with drag and drop, quick add, a detail panel, search, label filters and a compact view

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/task-board

- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/task-board.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/task-board`

### When to use

- Sprint and project boards in a product, with tasks moving through a few statuses
- Internal tools where people sort work by dragging it

### When not to use

- Touch-first apps – native drag and drop needs a mouse; offer the detail panel's status buttons instead

### Usage

```tsx
import { TaskBoard } from "@/components/ui/task-board";

export function Sprint({ tasks }) {
  return (
    <TaskBoard
      tasks={tasks}
      statuses={statuses}
      labels={labels}

      path={["Northwind", "Launch", "Sprint 12"]}
      onChange={save}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tasks | `Task[]` |  | key, title, status, priority (0–4), estimate, labels, assignee, dueIn, subtasks, pullRequest, created |
| statuses | `TaskStatus[]` |  | Columns in order: id, label and icon |
| labels | `TaskLabel[]` |  | id, label and color – used on cards, in the filter and in the panel |
| people | `TaskPerson[]` |  | id, name and avatar for assignees |
| path | `string[]` |  | Breadcrumb above the board |
| onChange | `(tasks: Task[]) => void` |  | Called with all tasks after every move, edit, add or delete |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Move through the toolbar, columns and cards
- Enter / Space: Open the focused card in the detail panel
- Escape: Close the detail panel or cancel a new task

### Accessibility

- Every card is focusable and opens a panel where status, priority, labels and assignee are plain toggle buttons – no dragging needed
- The star, compact view and filter are pressed or checked toggles; the breadcrumb marks the current page

### Motion

- Cards fade in, a blue line shows where a dragged card lands, the panel slides in from the right
- Reduced motion turns these off

### Responsive

- Columns keep a minimum width and the board scrolls sideways on narrow screens
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

## Testimonial Wall (Free)

The landing-page wall of quotes – columns that scroll endlessly in opposite directions, ease to a stop on hover and scrub with inertia

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/blocks/testimonial-wall
- Section: Blocks · Social proof
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/testimonial-wall.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/testimonial-wall`

### When to use

- A “Loved by” section on a landing or pricing page with eight or more quotes
- Social proof that should feel alive without asking for attention – it runs slowly and stops the moment someone reads

### When not to use

- Two or three quotes – show them side by side; a loop of three repeats too obviously
- A single hero quote or a case study – it deserves a static, larger layout
- Reviews people need to search or filter – use a list or grid

### Usage

```tsx
import { TestimonialWall } from "@/components/ui/testimonial-wall";

const items = [
  {
    quote: "We replaced three half-finished internal kits with it in a sprint.",
    name: "Lena Hartmann",
    role: "Design Lead",
    company: "Fieldnote",
    avatar: "/avatars/lena.jpg",
    rating: 5,
  },
  {
    quote: "The motion is the part nobody notices – which is exactly the point.",
    name: "Jonas Weber",
    role: "Staff Engineer",
    company: "Ledgerline",
    verified: true,
  },
  // … at least two quotes per column, ideally four or more
];

export function Testimonials() {
  return (
    <section className="py-24">
      <p className="text-center text-sm text-neutral-500">Testimonials</p>
      <h2 className="mb-10 text-center text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight">Loved by product teams</h2>
      <TestimonialWall items={items} speed={26} className="[--ui-tw-height:640px]" />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `{ quote, name, role?, company?, avatar?, rating?, verified? }[]` |  | The quotes. avatar is a photo URL – without one the initials sit on a soft gray circle. rating (1–5) adds a small gray star row, verified a gray check beside the name |
| columns | `1 \| 2 \| 3` | `3` | Most columns on a wide container; the wall itself drops to 2 below 740px and 1 below 480px of its own width |
| speed | `number` | `28` | Pixels per second of the first column; the others run about 15 % slower and faster, in alternating directions |
| pauseOnHover | `boolean` | `true` | Ease the hovered column to a stop and wind it back up on leave. Keyboard focus always stops its column |
| label | `string` | `"What customers say"` | Accessible name of the wall |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the wrapper. Set the height with --ui-tw-height (600px by default) and the edge fade with --ui-tw-fade (96px) |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves through the quotes; the focused card's column stops and the card is nudged into view
- Shift / Tab: Moves back; leaving the wall lets the columns run again

### Accessibility

- A labelled region; every quote is a figure with a blockquote and a figcaption, read out once – the copies that make the loop are aria-hidden and inert
- Keyboard focus stops the column, so a card never runs away from the focus ring
- Hover, focus and press-and-hold all stop the motion, which covers the WCAG pause requirement for moving content
- Star ratings are an image with a text label (“Rated 5 out of 5”), the check is labelled “Verified customer”
- Reduced motion shows every quote once in a static masonry grid

### Motion

- Each column repeats a measured set and wraps by exactly its height – no gap, no jump
- Columns alternate up and down at slightly different speeds and start at different points, so rows never line up
- One requestAnimationFrame loop eases a velocity per column: hover slows it to a stop over about a third of a second, leaving winds it back up
- Drag a column with the mouse to scrub it; letting go flings it with inertia before it settles back into its own pace
- The hovered card lifts 3px with a soft shadow while the rest of the wall dims a little
- Only runs while on screen; top and bottom edges fade out with a mask

### Responsive

- Columns follow the wall's own width (3 / 2 / 1), so it works in a sidebar as well as full width
- One column on phones with 15px quotes; names win over role and company when space is tight – down to 320px without overflow
- Touch: vertical swipes keep scrolling the page (no scroll trap); pressing and holding a column pauses it to read
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: logo-marquee, tilt-card, text-reveal

## Agent Team (Free)

A prompt types itself and branches out into three agents, each with a role and overlapping tool logos

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/agent-team
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/agent-team.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/agent-team`

### When to use

- AI and automation products where one prompt sets up several agents or roles
- Feature cards about teams, delegation or workflows that span several tools

### When not to use

- Real org charts or live agent status – the scene is decorative and loops on its own
- More than three agents – the layout is built for exactly three

### Usage

```tsx
import { AgentTeam } from "@/components/ui/agent-team";

export function FeatureCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 560 }}>
      <AgentTeam
        prompt="Build a team to work my inbound pipeline"
        members={[
          { role: "Lead Researcher", avatar: "/team/lena.jpg", tools: ["linkedin", "hubspot"] },
          { role: "Inbound Qualifier", avatar: "/team/theo.jpg", tools: ["hubspot", "slack"] },
          { role: "Outbound SDR", avatar: "/team/noah.jpg", tools: ["gmail", "salesforce"] },
        ]}
      />
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prompt | `string` | `"Build a team to work my inbound pipeline"` | Text that types itself into the prompt pill |
| members | `[AgentTeamMember, AgentTeamMember, AgentTeamMember]` |  | Required. Three agents, left to right – { role, avatar, tools? } with up to two of linkedin, hubspot, slack, gmail, salesforce |
| label | `string` |  | Accessible description – by default built from the prompt and the roles |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a label built from the prompt and the roles; everything inside is hidden from screen readers
- Nothing in the scene is interactive

### Motion

- The prompt types itself, the send button presses and a soft pink-to-violet glow blooms behind it, dashed lines draw down and the three agents pop in one after another – then it starts over
- Each status dot pops in last; the tool circles overlap slightly
- With prefers-reduced-motion it shows the finished team and stays still

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – text and shapes are sized in container units
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

---

## Cover Flow (Free)

Browse covers in 3D – drag, flick or scrub the row, it springs to the nearest cover; images drift in their frames over a soft reflection

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/cover-flow
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/cover-flow.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/cover-flow`

### When to use

- Six to twenty visual items where looking at one at a time is the point – albums, places, products, case studies, templates
- A showcase row that should feel physical: drag, flick, sideways trackpad scroll

### When not to use

- Text-heavy slides or many items to compare side by side – use a plain carousel or a grid
- Large libraries – a grid with a lightbox scales better

### Usage

```tsx
import { CoverFlow } from "@/components/ui/cover-flow";

export function Albums() {
  return (
    <CoverFlow
      aria-label="New releases"
      items={[
        { id: 1, title: "Low Tide", subtitle: "Mara Lind", image: "/covers/low-tide.jpg" },
        { id: 2, title: "Night Drive", subtitle: "Okto", image: "/covers/night-drive.jpg" },
        { id: 3, title: "Paper Moon", subtitle: "Ilse & June", image: "/covers/paper-moon.jpg" },
      ]}
      onSelect={(item) => openAlbum(item.id)}
    />
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `CoverFlowItem[]` |  | { id, title?, subtitle?, image?, alt?, cover? } – pass an image URL or any ReactNode as cover |
| index | `number` |  | Controlled front cover – pair with onIndexChange |
| defaultIndex | `number` | `middle cover` | Starting cover when uncontrolled |
| onIndexChange | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called whenever a different cover reaches the front, also while dragging |
| onSelect | `(item, index) => void` |  | Clicking the front cover or pressing Enter – e.g. open a detail view |
| itemWidth | `number` | `280` | Cover width in px – the whole row scales down in narrow containers (to half at most) |
| itemHeight | `number` | `280` | Cover height in px |
| angle | `number` | `50` | How far the side covers turn away, in degrees |
| reflection | `boolean` | `true` | Mirror the covers on the floor |
| caption | `boolean` | `true` | Title and subtitle of the front cover |
| renderCaption | `(item, index) => ReactNode` |  | Replaces the default caption |
| controls | `boolean` | `true` | Previous and next buttons beside the caption |
| ticks | `boolean` | `true` | Small position ticks under the caption – clicking one jumps there |
| sound | `boolean` | `false` | A soft click each time a new cover reaches the front (Web Audio, no file) |
| aria-label | `string` | `"Cover flow"` | Names the carousel |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Keyboard

- ← / →: Previous or next cover while the row has focus
- Home / End: First or last cover
- ↵: Selects the front cover (calls onSelect)

### Accessibility

- A region with aria-roledescription="carousel"; each cover is a group with aria-roledescription="slide" and a label like "3 of 10: Alpenglow"
- Covers away from the front are aria-hidden; the reflections are aria-hidden and inert
- The caption is a polite live region, so the new front cover is announced
- Previous / next are real buttons; the ticks are labelled "Show <title>" with aria-current and stay out of the tab order

### Motion

- A spring carries the row: drag 1:1, flick and it travels with your speed, then lands on a cover – a quick flick always moves at least one
- Sideways trackpad scrolling scrubs the row and settles in the direction of the swipe; vertical scrolling stays with the page
- Covers turn, recede, scale down and dim with distance; a light sheen sits on the side facing the center and each image drifts inside its frame
- The ends rubber-band; the caption rises in from the direction of travel
- With prefers-reduced-motion covers jump into place and the drift is off

### Responsive

- Scales with its container down to half size; touch-action pan-y keeps vertical swipes scrolling the page
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: tilt-card, logo-marquee, segmented-control

---

## DACH Region (Free)

DACH map with fading neighbours and a pastel band along the border, switchable to the US, China, India, Brazil or Japan

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/region-dach
- Section: Illustrations · Maps
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/region-dach.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/region-dach`

### When to use

- Showing a service area, sales territory or market focus in Germany, Austria and Switzerland
- Sections about regional exclusivity or local presence in one of the larger markets (US, China, India, Brazil, Japan), next to a short text

### When not to use

- Maps that need cities, regions or exact borders – the shapes are simplified and there are no labels

### Usage

```tsx
import { RegionDach } from "@/components/ui/region-dach";

export function TerritorySection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 420 }}>
      <RegionDach />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| region | `"dach" \| "us" \| "cn" \| "in" \| "br" \| "jp"` |  | Shown region (controlled). Pair it with onRegionChange to keep the menu working |
| defaultRegion | `Region` | `"dach"` | Region shown first when region is not set |
| onRegionChange | `(region: Region) => void` |  | Called when the viewer picks a region in the menu |
| showSwitcher | `boolean` | `true` | Show the region menu in the top-left corner |
| label | `string \| ((region: Region) => string)` | `"Map of the DACH region: Germany, Austria and Switzerland" / "Map of Japan" …` | Accessible description of the map; by default it follows the current region |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the menu button: open the region list. In the list: pick the highlighted region
- ArrowDown / ArrowUp: On the menu button: open the list. In the list: move through the regions
- Home / End: Jump to the first or last region
- Escape: Close the list and return focus to the menu button
- Tab: Close the list and move on

### Accessibility

- The map is one image whose label names the current region; the shapes inside are hidden from screen readers
- The menu button reports the current region and its expanded state; the list is a listbox with options, the selected one marked with aria-selected

### Motion

- A soft pastel band travels along the outer border in a continuous 14-second loop: a blurred glow that only spreads outwards, with three sharp layers on top
- Switching regions fades and slightly grows the old map away while the new one settles in from slightly smaller; the band starts anew
- The menu morphs open out of its button, and the hover fill glides between rows
- With prefers-reduced-motion the band stays still, regions swap instantly and the menu opens without the morph

### Responsive

- Transparent background; the neighbouring countries fade out towards the edges, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 540 : 440 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – set a width or max-width via className
- The menu scales down with the illustration (to about 60 %) so it still fits in small previews
- The file embeds the map data for all six regions (about 155 KB)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Frost Cloud (Free)

A frosted white cloud with eyes cut out of it, on a red-orange or blue sky – it floats, turns to look around, blinks, follows the pointer and bounces with a wink when clicked

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/frost-cloud
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/frost-cloud.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/frost-cloud`

### When to use

- A friendly face for an assistant, an AI feature or a cloud product – as an app icon, an empty state or a feature card
- Landing pages that want a calm, living mascot instead of a static logo

### When not to use

- Tiny sizes below ~48px – the glow and the eyes get lost
- Brands far from blue or orange – the colors are part of the look

### Usage

```tsx
import { FrostCloud } from "@/components/ui/frost-cloud";

export function AssistantCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 320 }}>
      <FrostCloud color="blue" />
      <h3>Meet your assistant</h3>
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| color | `"blue" \| "orange"` | `"orange"` | Blue-to-cyan or red-to-orange sky; the cloud's colors follow |
| background | `boolean` | `true` | Fill the whole box with the sky gradient; false leaves the cloud on a transparent background with a soft colored edge |
| followPointer | `boolean` | `true` | The eyes follow the pointer while it's over the illustration |
| label | `string` |  | Accessible description of the illustration |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label
- Clicking only plays an animation – nothing else happens

### Motion

- Frosted white and a little see-through, the sky shining through softly towards the bottom, eyes cut out of it
- The cloud floats and breathes; its shadow shrinks and fades as it rises
- Every few seconds it glances left, right, up or down: the body tilts a little, the eyes move further and the shine slides the other way, so it seems to turn
- It blinks at random moments, sometimes twice
- The eyes follow the pointer; a click gives a squishy bounce and a wink
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion it keeps still and only reacts to clicks

### Responsive

- Square by default; give it a height and the sky fills the whole box while the cloud stays centered, up to 320px wide
- Light and dark mode via a .dark class or data-theme="dark": a deeper sky in dark mode

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: glow-cloud, model-wheel

---

- Import: `@/components/ui/ghosted-chat`

- A problem card about cold outreach that gets ignored or messages left on read
- Bento grids and feature cards that need a small illustration above the text

- A real chat UI – the bubbles are a fixed, decorative scene
- Very small sizes below ~220px wide, where the bubble text gets hard to read

### Usage

```tsx
import { GhostedChat } from "@/components/ui/ghosted-chat";
```

### Accessibility

- The hover reply is purely decorative, nothing needs to be reached with the keyboard

### Motion

- A red shine sweeps through the last message every few seconds; the last bubble has a soft colored glow
- On hover the status texts fade out, the messages move up and a blue thumbs-down reply pops in with a small bounce
- With prefers-reduced-motion the shine stops and hover changes happen instantly

## Glow Keyboard (Pro)

AI chat input that types itself over a glass keyboard – every key press sends a wave up the gradient floor

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/glow-keyboard
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/glow-keyboard.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/glow-keyboard`

### When to use

- Hero sections for AI assistants, chat or writing tools – the prompt types itself and invites people to try
- Landing pages that want an interactive scene instead of a video

### When not to use

- As your real chat input – it is a showcase; use Chat Composer for a working input
- Small cards on mobile – the keyboard legends get tiny below ~360px width

### Usage

```tsx
import { GlowKeyboard } from "@/components/ui/glow-keyboard";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 1100, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <GlowKeyboard />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prompts | `string[]` | `three hiking prompts` | Prompts the demo types one after another; each one is sent with Enter |
| placeholder | `string` | `"Ask AI anything..."` | Placeholder of the chat input |
| onSubmit | `(text: string) => void` |  | Called when a prompt is sent with Enter – by the demo or the user |
| label | `string` | `"AI chat input above a glass keyboard…"` | Accessible name of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Click: Anywhere on the scene puts the cursor into the input and stops the demo
- Any key: Types and lights up the same key on the drawn keyboard
- Enter: Sends the prompt and clears the input

### Accessibility

- The input is a real text field with a label; the drawn keyboard and the floor are hidden from screen readers
- The demo stops as soon as the input gets focus, so it never types over the user

### Motion

- The demo types each prompt with an uneven, human rhythm, holds Shift for capitals and corrects one typo
- Every key press: the key sinks in, a wave rises out of the gradient below it and the input glow flashes at the same spot
- The floor's two layers – colour and white plus-lighter – drift and morph slowly
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion the scene stays still and the demo does not type, typing yourself still works

### Responsive

- Keeps an 11 : 6 frame and scales to the width of its container – every detail is sized in container units
- Set the background with --ui-gk-bg (default #fafafa, #111113 in dark mode)
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: gradient-floor, chat-composer

## Integration Beam (Free)

Your product between the tools it connects – light pulses flow along curved beams, hover to focus a tool, click to pause it

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/integration-beam
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-beam.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-beam`

### When to use

- A hero or integrations section that shows your product sitting between the tools a team already uses
- Landing pages where a calm, self-playing data flow explains “we connect to X and Y” faster than a logo wall

### When not to use

- A real integration settings page – pausing a tool here is only part of the scene, nothing is saved
- More than four tools per side – the beams get crowded; use Integration Grid or Logo Cluster for long lists

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationBeam } from "@/components/ui/integration-beam";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <IntegrationBeam />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| left | `{ name: string; logo: ReactNode }[]` | `Slack, Notion, Gmail` | Tools that send data in – on the left, or above the hub on narrow widths. The logo fills a 28 × 28 box |
| right | `{ name: string; logo: ReactNode }[]` | `HubSpot, Linear, Google Drive` | Tools that receive data – on the right, or below the hub on narrow widths |
| center | `{ name: string; logo?: ReactNode }` | `{ name: "Acme" }` | Your product. The logo is drawn white into a 36 × 36 box on the dark tile (currentColor); a neutral flower mark when left out |
| label | `string` | `"Acme connected to Slack, Notion, …"` | Accessible name of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves between the tool tiles; the focused tool's beam comes forward and its name shows
- Enter / Space: Pauses or reconnects the focused tool

### Accessibility

- The scene is a labelled group; every tool is a toggle button with aria-pressed and a name like “Slack, connected”
- Pausing or reconnecting is announced in a polite live region, with the new count (“5 of 6 connected”)
- The beams, pulses and logos are decorative and hidden from screen readers
- Visible focus ring on the tiles; the tooltip also shows on keyboard focus

### Motion

- Sync cycles: pulses leave the left tools 280 ms apart, travel 1.5 s along their beam and, as they land, the hub glows and the next wave leaves for the right tools
- Each pulse is a short gradient – clear tail, accent body, pale tip – with a soft blurred glow; one accent color only
- The status chip under the hub slides between “Syncing…” and “6 connected”, and its width glides with the text
- When the layout switches between side by side and stacked, the tiles glide to their new spots and the curves morph with them (460 ms)
- The loop only runs while the scene is on screen (IntersectionObserver)
- With prefers-reduced-motion the beams are drawn as static lines – no pulses, no glides; hover, focus and pausing still work

### Responsive

- The beams are measured from the real tile positions (ResizeObserver), so the scene reflows with its container
- Below 460px of container width the senders stack above the hub and the receivers below, with vertical beams; fits 320px screens
- On touch screens a tap pauses a tool and shows its name for a moment instead of a hover tooltip
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: integration-grid, integration-flow, logo-cluster, agent-team

---

## Integration Flow (Pro)

Integration pills rotating along a dashed arc, each beaming its data into a central analysis hub

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/integration-flow
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-flow.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-flow`

### When to use

- A hero or feature section that shows your product pulling data in from the tools teams already use
- Integration or data-platform pages where a short, self-playing loop explains the idea better than a logo wall

### When not to use

- A real list of connected integrations – the pills are decorative, not interactive
- Very small spaces below ~320px wide, where the pill text gets hard to read
- Brands that clash with the warm coral background

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationFlow } from "@/components/ui/integration-flow";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 1100, margin: "0 auto" }}>
      <IntegrationFlow />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `{ name: string; icon: ReactNode; title?: string; mono?: boolean }[]` | `Okta, Snowflake, Slack, ClickUp, Zendesk` | Integrations that rotate through the pills (5 or more look best). The icon fills a 64 × 64 box; mono logos turn black in the centre |
| label | `string` | `"Integrations like Slack, Okta and Snowflake…"` | Accessible description of the scene |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- The scene is exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the pills and cards inside are hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The pills travel along the dashed arc one slot at a time (0.9 s); the one landing in the centre turns light and shows its logo in color
- The centre pill charges up, a beam sweeps over to the Data Analysis hub (1.1 s) and the hub lights up as it arrives
- The coral background blobs drift and breathe slowly on a 16 s loop
- With prefers-reduced-motion everything stands still in the centre state, with the beam drawn in

### Responsive

- Drawn on a 2400 × 1490 stage and scaled to the width of its container, so the layout never reflows
- Keeps its 2400 : 1490 aspect ratio; set a width or max-width via className
- Set --ui-if-bg and --ui-if-fade to change the stage background and the color the bottom fades into
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

---

## Integration Grid (Free)

Honeycomb-like wall of integration logos around a bright centre tile with your product mark, fading out toward the edges

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/integration-grid
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/integration-grid.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/integration-grid`

### When to use

- Integration sections and feature cards like “Works with the tools you already use”
- Landing pages that show your product at the centre of an ecosystem

### When not to use

- A real, clickable list of integrations – the tiles are decorative and not links
- More than 22 logos – the grid has 22 outer tiles, extra logos are left out

### Usage

```tsx
import { IntegrationGrid } from "@/components/ui/integration-grid";

export function IntegrationsSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 760 }}>
      <IntegrationGrid mark={<img src="/logo.svg" alt="" width={40} height={40} />} />
      <h3>Plays well with your stack</h3>
      <p>Connect the tools your team already relies on.</p>
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| logos | `IntegrationGridLogo[]` | `22 well-known tools` | Logos filled row by row around the centre – each { name, path, color?, darkColor? } with a single 24 × 24 SVG path (e.g. from simple-icons); without color the mark follows the ink color |
| mark | `ReactNode` | `a neutral flower mark` | Content of the larger centre tile – usually your product logo |
| columns | `5 \| 7 \| 9` | `9` | Tiles in the middle row – the rows above and below get two fewer. Fewer columns make the tiles larger |
| label | `string` |  | Accessible description – by default lists the integrations |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image whose label lists every integration; tiles and logos are hidden from screen readers
- Nothing in the scene is interactive

### Motion

- Still by default; on hover a tile turns fully white and its logo grows a little from the centre
- With prefers-reduced-motion the hover lift is switched off

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 1520 : 560 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – every size is in container units
- Tile fills fade toward the edges while the logos keep their full brand colors
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Layer Stack (Free)

Isometric stack of five layers with a list beside it – the chosen entry lifts its layer out in color

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/layer-stack
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/layer-stack.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/layer-stack`

### When to use

- Explaining a layered product or platform – each entry is one layer of the stack
- Feature sections that walk through capabilities one by one, with a visual that follows along

### When not to use

- More than five layers – the stack and the list are sized for up to five
- Navigation that changes page content – this is an illustration with its own small state

### Usage

```tsx
import { LayerStack } from "@/components/ui/layer-stack";

export function PlatformSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <LayerStack
        items={[
          { title: "Triggered by events", hint: "Webhooks", icon: "bolt" },
          { title: "Grounded in your data", hint: "Context", icon: "database" },
          { title: "Connected to your apps", hint: "APIs", icon: "plug" },
          { title: "Works with any model", hint: "Routing", icon: "spark" },
          { title: "Traced at every step", hint: "Logs", icon: "pulse" },
        ]}
      />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | `LayerStackItem[]` | `five sample layers` | Up to five entries, top layer first – { title, hint?, icon? } with icon one of bolt, database, plug, spark, pulse |
| defaultIndex | `number` | `0` | Entry to start on |
| interval | `number` | `2600` | Time per entry while it plays on its own, in ms |
| onChange | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called when the user picks an entry |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Tab: Moves focus to the chosen entry
- ↑ / ↓: Picks the previous or next entry

### Accessibility

- The list is a vertical tablist with real buttons; the chosen entry has aria-selected
- The stack itself is decorative and hidden from screen readers

### Motion

- The chosen layer and the ones above it glide up to open a gap; its face, edge and icon turn blue and a soft glow fades in beneath it
- A white card glides behind the chosen entry in the list
- Steps through the entries on its own and pauses while hovered or focused; after a click or key press it stays put
- With prefers-reduced-motion it doesn't play on its own and changes happen instantly

### Responsive

- Transparent background, so it sits on any light or dark surface
- Keeps a 3 : 2 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – text and layers are sized in container units
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

## Model Wheel (Free)

AI model names on a turning drum – the rows bend away at the edges and each model lands on a soft gray fill

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/model-wheel
- Section: Illustrations · Card illustrations
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/model-wheel.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/model-wheel`

### When to use

- Feature cards about model choice, routing or "bring your own model"
- Landing pages that list supported AI providers in a calm, moving way

### When not to use

- A real model picker – the wheel can be spun, but it doesn't report a choice
- Long lists – the drum shows about seven rows at a time

### Usage

```tsx
import { ModelWheel } from "@/components/ui/model-wheel";

export function FeatureCard() {
  return (
    <article style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <ModelWheel />
      <h3>Every model, one workspace</h3>
    </article>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| models | `{ name, viewBox, color, d }[]` | `8 popular models` | Models on the wheel, each with its brand mark as one SVG path; use at least 7 to keep the drum full |
| hold | `number` | `1500` | Milliseconds a model stays in the middle |
| label | `string` | `"AI models on a turning wheel…"` | Accessible description of the illustration |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- Exposed as one image with a descriptive label; the rows are hidden from screen readers
- Hovering holds the wheel, so nothing moves while someone reads it
- Spinning by hand also works with touch; the automatic turn starts again after a short pause

### Motion

- The rows sit on a cylinder: towards the top and bottom they tilt away, shrink and fade
- Every turn runs on a soft spring: the drum gathers speed, overshoots a touch and locks onto the next model like a magnet
- Grab the wheel and drag it up or down to spin it; a quick flick keeps it turning, then it snaps onto the closest model
- The wheel turns downwards; the model in the middle sits on a gray fill that grows or shrinks to its name
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion it doesn't turn by itself, but can still be spun by hand

### Responsive

- Fixed height of seven rows; the width follows its container
- Light and dark mode via a .dark class or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Brand marks belong to their owners – check you may show them before you ship

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: glow-keyboard, chat-composer

## Voice Orb (Pro)

The face of a voice assistant – a sphere of dots that breathes, catches sound, collapses into a spinning ring while thinking and ripples when it speaks

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/voice-orb
- Section: Illustrations · Product scenes
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/voice-orb.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/voice-orb`

### When to use

- Voice mode of an assistant: one calm object that shows whether the AI listens, thinks or talks
- Hero of an AI product page, an empty state before the first prompt, or a call screen
- Anywhere a spinner would undersell what is happening – the orb says which phase it is

### When not to use

- Inline in a chat thread or next to text – use Thinking Loader or Thinking State, they are made for small sizes
- As decoration that never changes state – a still image costs nothing; the orb draws every frame
- Below about 96px – the dots merge into a blob

### Usage

```tsx
import { VoiceOrb } from "@/components/ui/voice-orb";

export function VoiceMode() {
  const { state, level, toggle } = useVoiceSession(); // "idle" | "listening" | "thinking" | "speaking", 0–1
  return <VoiceOrb state={state} level={level} onPress={toggle} />;
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| state | `"idle" \| "listening" \| "thinking" \| "speaking"` | `"idle"` | What the assistant is doing – the orb melts from one state into the next |
| level | `number` |  | Loudness from 0 to 1 while listening or speaking. Without it the orb makes up a natural-looking level |
| size | `number` | `220` | Edge length in px |
| dots | `number` | `520` | Number of dots – raise it for large sizes |
| accent | `string` | `blue` | Color the moving dots take on; resting dots use the text color |
| label | `boolean \| Partial<Record<state, string>>` | `true` | The line under the orb – false hides it, an object replaces single texts |
| interactive | `boolean` | `true` | Dots give way to the mouse pointer |
| onPress | `() => void` |  | Makes the orb a button, e.g. to start and stop listening |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |
| style | `CSSProperties` |  | Inline styles on the root – set color here to change the resting dots |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: With onPress: presses the orb

### Accessibility

- The canvas is decorative; the state is in the label, which is announced politely when it changes
- With onPress the orb is a real button named by its label; without it, an image named after the state
- With prefers-reduced-motion nothing moves: the orb shows one still frame per state (sphere, raised dots, ring, waves)
- The colors follow the text color and adapt to dark mode on their own

### Motion

- Idle: the sphere turns slowly and breathes
- Listening: dots jump outward with the level and take on the accent color; a soft glow follows the loudness
- Thinking: the sphere collapses into a tilted, fast spinning ring with a light running around it
- Speaking: waves travel from pole to pole with the level
- States are blended, never switched – every dot glides from one shape to the next in about a third of a second
- The animation pauses while the orb is off screen or the tab is in the background

### Responsive

- Fixed square of size px – pass a smaller size on phones; it is sharp on high-density screens
- Touch screens: no pointer effect, the press works as usual
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Notes for AI

- Changing state or level never restarts the animation – only size and dots rebuild the canvas
- Smooth a raw microphone level a little before passing it, or pass it as is: the orb eases towards it anyway

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: thinking-loader, thinking-state, chat-composer

---

## World Map Continental (Pro)

World map with one highlighted continent and a pastel band along its coastline, switchable between all six

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/illustrations/world-map
- Section: Illustrations · Maps
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/world-map.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/world-map`

### When to use

- Showing that you serve, operate in or focus on one continent
- Market, coverage or expansion sections on a landing page, where a calm map says more than a list of countries

### When not to use

- Data maps with values per country – this is a decorative illustration, not a chart
- Showing individual countries – each continent is one merged shape without borders, simplified from Natural Earth 1:110m

### Usage

```tsx
import { WorldMap } from "@/components/ui/world-map";

export function MarketSection() {
  return (
    <section style={{ maxWidth: 640 }}>
      <WorldMap />
    </section>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| continent | `"north-america" \| "south-america" \| "europe" \| "africa" \| "asia" \| "oceania"` |  | Highlighted continent (controlled). Pair it with onContinentChange to keep the menu working |
| defaultContinent | `Continent` | `"europe"` | Continent highlighted first when continent is not set |
| onContinentChange | `(continent: Continent) => void` |  | Called when the viewer picks a continent in the menu |
| showSwitcher | `boolean` | `true` | Show the continent menu in the top-left corner |
| label | `string \| ((continent: Continent) => string)` | `"World map with Europe highlighted" …` | Accessible description of the map; by default it follows the current continent |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for width or margins |

### Keyboard

- Enter / Space: On the menu button: open the continent list. In the list: pick the highlighted continent
- ArrowDown / ArrowUp: On the menu button: open the list. In the list: move through the continents
- Home / End: Jump to the first or last continent
- Escape: Close the list and return focus to the menu button
- Tab: Close the list and move on

### Accessibility

- The map is one image whose label names the highlighted continent; the shapes inside are hidden from screen readers
- The menu button reports the current continent and its expanded state; the list is a listbox with options, the selected one marked with aria-selected

### Motion

- A soft pastel band travels along the coastline of the continent's main landmass in a continuous 14-second loop: a blurred glow that only spreads outwards, with three sharp layers on top – the same band as in the DACH Region map
- Switching continents fades the old highlight back into the gray world while the new one settles in from slightly smaller with its shadow; the band starts anew
- The menu morphs open out of its button, and the hover fill glides between rows
- With prefers-reduced-motion the band stays still, continents swap instantly and the menu opens without the morph

### Responsive

- Transparent background; the solid gray world and the lighter highlighted continent read on light and dark surfaces alike
- Keeps a 540 : 242 aspect ratio and scales to the width of its container – set a width or max-width via className
- The menu scales down with the illustration (to about 60 %); on small sizes the open list may extend below the map
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

---

## Blur Crossfade (Pro)

Swaps content with a soft blur while the box glides smoothly to the size of what comes next

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/blur-crossfade
- Section: Motion · Transitions
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/blur-crossfade.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/blur-crossfade`

### When to use

- Button labels and status text that change in place – Save → Saving… → Saved
- Panels, tips or steps that swap content of different lengths without a jump in the layout

### When not to use

- Navigating between pages or large views – use a route transition instead
- Content that updates many times per second, like counters or live prices

### Usage

```tsx
import { BlurCrossfade } from "@/components/ui/blur-crossfade";

export function SaveButton({ status }) {
  return (
    <button>
      <BlurCrossfade id={status} morph="both" as="span">
        {status === "saving" ? "Saving…" : status === "saved" ? "Saved" : "Save"}
      </BlurCrossfade>
    </button>
  );
}

// Height glides between messages of different length
<BlurCrossfade id={step}>
  <p>{steps[step]}</p>
</BlurCrossfade>
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| id | `string \| number` |  | Key of the current content – changing it starts the swap |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content for the current id |
| duration | `number` | `420` | Length of the swap and the size morph in ms |
| blur | `number` | `10` | Blur in px at the outer ends of the fade |
| morph | `"height" \| "both" \| "none"` | `"height"` | Which sides glide to the new size; both makes the box as wide as its content |
| as | `"div" \| "span"` | `"div"` | Root element – span inside buttons and other inline content |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the box |

### Accessibility

- Only the current content is exposed – the leaving copy is aria-hidden and inert
- Put aria-live on a surrounding element when the change should be announced, e.g. a status button

### Motion

- The old content blurs, fades and grows slightly as the new one sharpens in from 98 %, while the box glides to the new height (and width)
- Quick changes stay clean: only the latest leaving copy and the current content are ever on screen
- Reduced motion swaps instantly

### Responsive

- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"
- Content keeps its natural size; the box only clips during the swap, so shadows and focus rings show otherwise

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: text-reveal, gradient-text

---

## Gradient Floor (Pro)

A blurred colour gradient that glows up from the bottom edge – two layers that drift and morph

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/gradient-floor
- Section: Motion · Backgrounds
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/gradient-floor.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/gradient-floor`

### When to use

- Hero sections, AI features or call-to-action blocks that need a warm, living backdrop
- Behind a chat input or a prompt, to make it feel like the start of something

### When not to use

- Behind long body text – the bright floor competes with small type
- Several floors on one screen – each one runs its own animation

### Usage

```tsx
import { GradientFloor } from "@/components/ui/gradient-floor";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    // Give the floor a height, e.g. with a class
    <GradientFloor className="hero">
      <h1>Ideas start to glow</h1>
    </GradientFloor>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content rendered above the floor |
| colors | `[string, string, string]` | `["#FF7700", "#FF0055", "#0073FF"]` | Gradient from the crest down |
| speed | `number` | `3` | Seconds per morph loop; 0 keeps the shape still |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root, e.g. for height or rounded corners |

### Accessibility

- The floor layers are hidden from screen readers; only your children are announced
- Keep text above the bright part of the floor at a readable contrast

### Motion

- Two blurred layers – colour and a white plus-lighter layer – whose peaks and valleys rise and fall against each other
- Both layers drift sideways on the same beat, the light one a little less
- Runs only while on screen; with prefers-reduced-motion the floor stays still

### Responsive

- Scales with the width of its container and stays anchored to the bottom edge – give the root a height
- Set the background with --ui-gf-bg (default #fafafa, dark mode #111113)

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: glow-keyboard, grid-background

## Gradient Text (Pro)

Letters cut from a liquid, ever-flowing gradient – the color sweeps across the word the first time it's seen

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/gradient-text
- Section: Motion · Text
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/gradient-text.json` (needs the Pro access key)
- Import: `@/components/ui/gradient-text`

### When to use

- One word or a short phrase in a hero headline that should carry the brand
- A highlight inside a heading, like a product name or the payoff of a sentence

### When not to use

- Body copy or long passages – a moving gradient makes them harder to read
- Several highlights on one screen – the effect works because it's rare

### Usage

```tsx
import { GradientText } from "@/components/ui/gradient-text";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <h1>
      Interfaces people actually <GradientText>feel.</GradientText>
    </h1>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | The text to fill with the gradient |
| colors | `string[]` | `["#dd0674", "#5e3ee0", "#ff5fae", "#7c5cff"]` | Gradient start, end and up to two blob colors; replaces the dark-mode colors too |
| speed | `number` | `8` | Seconds per flow cycle |
| sweep | `boolean` | `true` | Sweep the color in from left to right when the text scrolls into view |
| as | `"span" \| "h1" \| "h2" \| "p"` | `"span"` | Element to render |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the root |

### Accessibility

- The text stays real, selectable text – the gradient copy on top is aria-hidden
- Pick colors with enough contrast against your background; the defaults are tuned for white and near-black

### Motion

- Soft color blobs drift across a two-color base in a slow loop; the sweep wipes the color in once, the first time the text is 60% visible
- Reduced motion shows the finished gradient, standing still

### Responsive

- Font, size and weight come from the parent, so it scales with your headline
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19

Related: text-reveal

## Grid Background (Free)

A fine line grid that drifts slowly behind your content and fades out towards the edges

- Page: https://www.affectui.com/motion/grid-background
- Section: Motion · Backgrounds
- Install: `npx shadcn@latest add https://www.affectui.com/r/grid-background.json`
- Import: `@/components/ui/grid-background`

### When to use

- Hero sections and feature headers that need a quiet, technical backdrop
- Empty states or panels that feel too flat on a plain background

### When not to use

- Behind dense text or data tables – the lines compete with the content
- Several moving backgrounds on one screen – keep it to one per view

### Usage

```tsx
import { GridBackground } from "@/components/ui/grid-background";

export function Hero() {
  return (
    <GridBackground size={48} direction="diagonal">
      <section style={{ display: "grid", placeItems: "center", minHeight: 480 }}>
        <h1>Build on a steady grid</h1>
      </section>
    </GridBackground>
  );
}
```

### Props

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | `ReactNode` |  | Content rendered above the grid |
| size | `number` | `48` | Cell size in px |
| color | `string` | `rgba(0,0,0,.07)` | Line color; dark mode defaults to rgba(255,255,255,.07) |
| speed | `number` | `3` | Seconds per cell; 0 keeps the grid still |
| direction | `"up" \| "down" \| "left" \| "right" \| "diagonal"` | `"diagonal"` | Drift direction; diagonal runs from top right to bottom left |
| reveal | `boolean` | `true` | Uncover the grid with a circle growing from the center when it first comes into view |
| fade | `number` | `70` | Radius of the edge fade, in % of the distance to the corners |
| className | `string` |  | Extra class on the container – give it a height or let the content size it |

### Accessibility

- The grid layer is decorative: aria-hidden and pointer-events: none
- Content sits in its own layer above the grid and stays fully interactive

### Motion

- The lines move by exactly one cell per loop, so the drift is seamless; only transform is animated
- The reveal grows a circular mask from the center once, when the grid is 20% in view
- Reduced motion: the grid stays still and appears without the reveal

### Responsive

- Fills its container at any size; the fade follows the container's shape
- Dark mode built in: switches when an ancestor (usually <html>) has the class dark or data-theme="dark"

### Requirements

- React 19
